summary: The principal island of the archipelago, whose streams rise in the central mountain range, flow torrentially and destructively in winter and shrink in summer through diversion into levadas. The Elucidário treats its irrigation system and levada laws, rural remedies, lichens, arachnids and limpets, and records the avocado grown in its lower zone and the cinnamon tree cultivated in quintas and gardens. It also forms the electoral district whose parliamentary representatives are listed.

summary: The capital of the archipelago and seat of the principal captaincy, where settlement began; it was made a vila c.1451–52. Its bay, the widest in the archipelago, lies between Ponta do Garajau and Ponta da Cruz and offers sheltered anchorage, though its harbour had never been studied oceanographically. The Elucidário discusses it as a health resort with climate data and records the January 1906 disturbances, the Danish prince's visit in May 1846 and recent volcanic cones in the area.

summary: A small uninhabited island group, politically part of the Madeira archipelago. The Elucidário covers its geography, geology, fauna, ownership history and legends of hidden treasure, including Shackleton's treasure plans, and notes the annual hunting of shearwaters and rabbits. summary: Campanário is a parish in Madeira, formerly part of Câmara de Lobos and later joined to the municipality of Ribeira Brava, drained by the Ribeira do Campanário (or da Lapa). The Elucidário records its landing, its band, its capitania-mor, its tithes paid to the Jesuits, a former chapel of St John founded in 1728, and the vicar sentenced by the Alçada of 1823. It was also the birthplace of Bishop D. Manuel Joaquim Gonçalves de Andrade and the jurist Francisco Justino Gonçalves de Andrade.
location: parish of Campanário, municipality of Ribeira Brava

summary: The Distrito do Funchal is the single administrative district covering the whole Madeira archipelago. The Elucidário cites its mortality statistics for 1917.

summary: Demerara, in British Guiana, received mass Madeiran emigration from about 1840, including emigrants after 1846, and was the main export market for Madeiran onions. The Elucidário also records it as the source of the dwarf banana, of entire-leaved sweet potatoes (1845) and of the ant Iridomyrmex humilis, and as the place where Alípio Augusto Ferreira edited O Portuguez.

summary: Trindade (Trinidad) was a destination of Madeiran emigrants after 1846. Editions of José Marciano da Silveira's pamphlet were made for its Madeiran colony.

summary: Guiné is an African coast recorded as the destination the discoverers of the archipelago were seeking when they were blown off course. The Elucidário also notes that Prince Henry ceded its temporal rule to the Crown, and that Daniel Telo Simões Soares fought there in 1891.

summary: The Índias Ocidentais (West Indies) were a major market for Madeira wine in the eighteenth century and the region of origin of the guava. Francis Masson visited them before returning to Madeira.

location: Funchal

location: beside the Chapel of Corpo Santo, Funchal

It contained the Casa de D. Guiomar, the military hospital's first site, and the provisional hospice that opened in 1853, and later housed the Clube Washington.

location: Rua do Castanheiro, Funchal

The building had been begun in 1905 under the Hohenlohe sanatorium concession and was enlarged in 1940; the hospital took in military patients from 1938.
location: Marmeleiros, parish of Monte, municipality of Funchal

The Elucidário records its churches, notable buildings, judicial role as starting point of the eastern comarca, and several notable people born there, and notes that the Bugio belongs to it administratively.

The council occupied a house there from 1838 that was damaged by the 1842 flood; it also held a passo of the Procissão dos Passos, the Talia society's premises, and was where Francisco Rodrigues Jardim was hanged in effigy.

location: Rua Direita, Funchal

summary: Rio de Janeiro, in Brazil, appears in the Elucidário as the seat of the Portuguese court and as a city where many Madeirans lived, studied, taught, published and died. Among them were Paulo Perestrelo da Câmara, João de Oliveira Sá Camelo Lampreia and João da Silveira Caldeira, who headed the Mint there.

summary: Ceuta is a fortress city in North Africa that was conquered in 1415 with the participation of the Order of Christ. The Elucidário records that João Gonçalves Zarco fought and was knighted there, and that members of the Câmara family fought in its defence when it was besieged. It was also the see of Nuno de Aguiar.

summary: The Campo do Duque was a large open ground at the centre of early Funchal belonging to the grand masters of the Order of Christ. It was granted for the building of the Sé (from 1485), the town hall and the square with its pillory, and the Terreiro da Sé was part of it. It is recorded as the site where sugar cane was first planted and where the first two-storey cedar house in Funchal was built.
location: Funchal, Madeira

location: sítio in the parish of Santo António, municipality of Funchal

summary: China is cited in the Elucidário as the country of origin of many plants grown in Madeira, including the tangerine, most bamboos, the apricot, the peach, the dwarf banana, the boganga and the cacho roxo. It is also named as one of the places where the palanquin was used to carry persons of rank.

It was once named after Gonçalo Aires and was renamed in 1922 in honour of Dr. António Aurélio da Costa Ferreira. The street housed the Hotel Miles and the headquarters of Miss Mary Jane Wilson's congregation, and the artillery company sent in 1917 was quartered there.
location: Funchal, Madeira

location: square at the sítio da Fonte, parish of Monte, municipality of Funchal

summary: The Capela do Senhor dos Milagres is a historic chapel on the Largo dos Milagres in Machico, formerly of Cristo or the Misericórdia. It is said to have been founded from the discoverers' vow at the landing site and is claimed to be Madeira's first church, a claim the Elucidário disputes. It was destroyed in the 1803 flood, when its image was found at sea by an American ship; it was later repaired by Roberto Page and is the centre of a pilgrimage on 9 October.
location: Largo dos Milagres, parish and municipality of Machico

The unfinished 1837 infant asylum there later became the Asilo da Mendicidade, and the town council occupied the building in 1843–45 and 1846–48. The cemetery holds a 1917 monument to victims of the German bombardment.

location: street between Largo dos Lavradores and Largo das Torneiras, Funchal, Madeira

name: Capelas das Almas Pobres
summary: A small rock-cut chapel of the Almas Pobres in Funchal, standing between the convents of Santa Clara and Mercês. It was built in 1781 by Roque José de Araujo and is tied to a local legend about the souls in purgatory. The Elucidário also mentions an older chapel of the same name in Santa Maria Maior parish, founded around 1470.
location: Between the convents of Santa Clara and Mercês, parish of São Pedro, Funchal

name: Cais em frente da entrada da Cidade
aliases: Cais em frente da entrada da Cidade
summary: The quay at the Entrada da Cidade in Funchal. A municipal stone quay begun there in 1843 failed. The state later built a quay, completed in 1892, and its extension was inaugurated in 1933.
location: Entrada da Cidade, Funchal

name: Cortina da Cidade
summary: The Cortina da Cidade was the circuit of walls that defended Funchal by land and sea. It was begun under D. Sebastião and completed in 1689. The Elucidário traces its construction and financing, and the gradual demolition of the walls and their gates in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
location: Funchal

name: Capelas de São Sebastião
summary: Chapels dedicated to Saint Sebastian in Ponta do Sol, Porto Santo, Santa Cruz and São Jorge. The Elucidário gives brief notes on them, including their rebuilding in the eighteenth century.
location: Parish and municipality of Ponta do Sol (among others)

name: Cemiterios
summary: The cemeteries of Funchal and Madeira, built from 1836 onwards to replace burial inside churches. The Elucidário gives a short history of them.
location: Parish of São Roque, Funchal

name: Ilhéus da Ceroulas
summary: Two small islets, do Guincho and das Ceroulas, lying off the coast of Seixal. They are also called the Seixal islets.
location: Off the coast of Seixal, municipality of Porto Moniz

name: Largo ou Praça dos Lavradores
summary: A square in Funchal on the left bank of the João Gomes stream. It was formerly the site of a Saturday fair selling poles and stakes for vine trellises. The main entrance of the Mercado dos Lavradores, opened in 1939, is on the square.
location: Left bank of the João Gomes stream, Funchal

name: Chicharos
summary: Chicharos is a sítio (locality) in the parish of Faial.
location: Sítio in the parish of Faial

name: Barreirinha
summary: A small beach in Funchal, east of the Santiago fortress and below the parish church of Santa Maria Maior. In 1939 Funchal council made it easily accessible as a bathing beach.
location: East of the Santiago fortress, parish of Santa Maria Maior, Funchal

name: Fonte do Barreiro
summary: A small spring near the foot of Pico Ruivo, at about 1,870 metres, which the Elucidário believed to be the highest spring in Madeira. Its water is clear and cold, but its flow is small in summer.
location: Near the foot of Pico Ruivo, at about 1,870 metres

name: Travessa do Porto Santo
summary: The Travessa is the popular name for the stretch of sea, about 27 miles long, between Madeira and Porto Santo. It runs from the Ilhéu de Fora off Ponta de São Lourenço to the Ilhéu de Baixo or da Cal. It is known for storms and generally rough seas.
location: Sea between the Ilhéu de Fora (Ponta de São Lourenço) and the Ilhéu de Baixo or da Cal (Porto Santo)

name: Capelas de São João Baptista
summary: Chapels dedicated to St John the Baptist in Madeira. Chief among them is the fifteenth-century São João da Ribeira chapel in Funchal, an early seat of the Franciscans. The Elucidário adds shorter notes on chapels of the same dedication in Ponta do Sol, Câmara de Lobos, Calheta, Campanário and Santana.

name: Igreja
summary: A locality in Monte parish containing the parish church and the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Conceição. Emperor Charles of Austria is buried in the parish church.
location: Sítio in the parish of Monte, municipality of Funchal

name: Igreja
summary: A locality in Quinta Grande parish. The chapel of Santo António, built in 1884 at the Quinta do Pombal, stands there.
location: Sítio in the parish of Quinta Grande

name: Avenida de Pedro Jose de Ornelas
summary: An avenue in Funchal, formerly the Caminho da Pena. It is named after a president of the municipal council who died in 1878.
location: Funchal

name: Carvalho de Araújo
summary: A street in Funchal, formerly Rua do Aljube. It was renamed in 1919 after the naval officer Carvalho de Araújo, who was killed in 1918 defending the steamer San Miguel.
location: Funchal

name: Mécia
summary: The Casa de Dona Mécia is an old building in the Rua dos Aranhas, Funchal. It formerly housed a teacher-training school and a Protestant chapel. It was classified as a property of public interest in 1940.
location: Rua dos Aranhas, Funchal

name: Convento de Nossa Senhora ds Piedade
aliases: Convento de Nossa Senhora ds Piedade
summary: A former Franciscan convent in Madeira founded by the Genoese settler Urbano Lomelino, who left his estate entailed to finish and maintain it. After the religious orders were abolished it returned to his heirs. No trace of it now survives.

name: Nossa Senhora da Fátima
summary: A chapel dedicated to Our Lady of Fátima at Pico do Galo, Câmara de Lobos. It was founded by Father António de Abreu Vieira and blessed in 1931.
location: Pico do Galo, parish and municipality of Câmara de Lobos

name: Capelas de Nossa Senhora da Fé
summary: Two chapels dedicated to Our Lady of Faith. One was founded in São Martinho in 1668. The other was built at Porto da Cruz in the 1820s and has since vanished.
location: São Martinho and Porto da Cruz

name: Capela de Nossa Senhora da Glória
summary: A chapel of Our Lady of Glory in Campanário. It was founded in 1599 and restored by the Countess of Torre Bela.
location: Campanário, municipality of Ribeira Brava

name: Capela de Nossa Senhora de Jesus
summary: The earliest known chapel of Our Lady of Jesus. It was founded in São Martinho in 1656 by João Bettencourt de Atouguia.
location: São Martinho, municipality of Funchal

name: Capelas de Nossa Senhora do Livramento
summary: Chapels of Our Lady of Deliverance in Caniço, Ponta do Sol, Monte, Estreito da Calheta and São Vicente. The Elucidário records their founders and dates, and notes that the Caniço chapel was a pilgrimage site.

name: Capelas de Santa Quitéria
summary: Three former chapels dedicated to Santa Quitéria in Madeira. They stood at Pico do Cardo in Santo António parish (1727), at Lombo da Estrela in Calheta (1724), and at Madalena do Mar.
location: Pico do Cardo, parish of Santo António, Funchal (among others)

name: Piedade
summary: Monte Gordo, or Piedade, is a seaward height in Caniçal parish. It is crowned by the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Piedade, a landmark for ships, said to have been founded in the 16th century by Garcia Moniz.
location: Height in the parish of Caniçal, municipality of Santa Cruz

name: Piedade
summary: Piedade is an inhabited locality in the parish of Jardim do Mar, Madeira. The Elucidário records there the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Piedade and the manor house of the Couto Cardoso entail, founded in 1730 and rebuilt in 1825.
location: sítio in the parish of Jardim do Mar, Madeira

name: Pimenta de Aguiar
summary: Rua Pimenta de Aguiar is a street in Funchal linking Rua da Carreira with Rua das Cruzes. It was named in 1895 in honour of the poet Manuel Caetano Pimenta de Aguiar.
location: street in Funchal, between Rua da Carreira and Rua das Cruzes

name: Ferreiros
summary: Ferreiros, also called Quinta dos Ferreiros, is a small locality in the parish of Calheta. A chapel of Nossa Senhora da Penha was built there in 1682.
location: sítio in the parish and municipality of Calheta, Madeira

name: Nossa Senhora Mãe dos Homens
summary: Nossa Senhora Mãe dos Homens is a chapel of Our Lady Mother of Men on the Caminho do Meio in the parish of Santa Maria Maior, Funchal. It was owned by the Visconde de Cacongo.
location: Caminho do Meio, parish of Santa Maria Maior, municipality of Funchal

name: Capelas de Nossa Senhora dos Milagres
summary: The Elucidário entry covers two chapels dedicated to Our Lady of Miracles on Madeira. One is in Monte (1661) and the other in Ponta do Sol (1662).
location: Monte (Funchal) and Ponta do Sol, Madeira

name: Capela de Nossa Senhora do Monserrate
summary: The Capela de Nossa Senhora do Monserrate was a chapel of Our Lady of Montserrat in Calheta. It stood near the old pillory and had long since disappeared.
location: near the old pillory of Calheta, municipality of Calheta

name: Santa Cruz
summary: Santa Cruz is a town and municipality in eastern Madeira, raised to the status of vila in 1515 within the captaincy of Machico. The Elucidário covers its customs house, its Misericórdia, its rivalry with Machico and later changes to its boundaries.
location: town and municipality of Santa Cruz, eastern Madeira

name: Santana
summary: Santana is a parish on Madeira's north coast, praised as the most picturesque of the north. It was created from São Jorge in the 16th century, and the entry covers its settlement, parish priests, church, localities and population.
location: parish of Santana, municipality of Santana, north coast of Madeira

name: Girão
summary: Cabo Girão is a sheer sea cliff on Madeira's south coast, about 600 metres high and among the tallest in the world. According to Frutuoso, its name marks the end of the first day's circuit of the discovery voyage. The entry also records a viewpoint built around 1935 and a public works director's account of the cliff's height.
location: south coast of Madeira

name: Funda
summary: This Ribeira Funda is a stream that rises at the Picos da Silva and da Relva. It forms the boundary between the parishes of Estreito da Calheta and Prazeres.
location: between the parishes of Estreito da Calheta and Prazeres, municipality of Calheta

name: Funda
summary: This Ribeira Funda is a stream in the municipality of Santana. It crosses the parish of São Jorge.
location: parish of São Jorge, municipality of Santana

name: Baixa do Furado
summary: The Baixa do Furado is a shoal off the coast of Achadas da Cruz.
location: off Achadas da Cruz, municipality of Porto Moniz

name: Ponte do Furado
summary: The Ponta do Furado is a coastal projection near Ponta de São Lourenço. It bounds the Abra inlet to the east.
location: east of the Abra inlet, near Ponta de São Lourenço, Madeira

name: Ilhéu de Branca
summary: The Ilhéu de Branca is a small islet at the eastern end of Madeira. It lies off the northern shore of the Ponta de São Lourenço.
location: off the northern shore of Ponta de São Lourenço, Madeira

name: Branca
summary: Ponta Branca, also called Ponta de Nordeste, is a headland on the north-east coast of Porto Santo.
location: north-east coast of Porto Santo

name: Boqueirão do Furado
summary: The Boqueirão do Furado is a small channel separating the tip of Ponta de São Lourenço from the Ilhéu de Agostinho. It can be forded at low tide.
location: between Ponta de São Lourenço and the Ilhéu de Agostinho, Madeira

name: Largo do Poço
summary: The Largo do Poço is a square in Funchal beside the Campo do Almirante Reis. It is notable for its ornamental fountain.
location: beside the Campo do Almirante Reis, Funchal

name: Poço Novo
summary: Poço Novo was the former name of the Funchal street now called Rua dos Tanoeiros. The Elucidário explains the name with a quotation from Frutuoso about a well at the end of the street.
location: Rua dos Tanoeiros, Funchal

name: Poços da Neve
summary: The Poços da Neve were man-made pits in Madeira's mountains used to store winter hail and snow. They supplied ice for sorbets in summer and are now abandoned.
location: mountains of Madeira

name: Capelas de Nossa Senhora da Conceição
summary: This entry surveys the chapels in Madeira dedicated to Our Lady of the Conception, from the 16th century to 1930, with their founders and dates. It includes the Capela-Monumento at Babosas, Monte, built in 1906 to mark the jubilee of the dogma of the Immaculate Conception.
location: various sites in Madeira, including Babosas, parish of Monte, municipality of Funchal

name: Lombada, Ribeira e Capela de São Pedro
aliases: São Pedro (Lombada, Ribeira e Capela de)
summary: The Lombada de São Pedro is a locality in the parish of Santa Cruz, crossed by a stream also called the Ribeira da Boaventura. The chapel of São Pedro was founded there in the early 16th century, destroyed by the flood of 1803 and rebuilt.
location: parish and municipality of Santa Cruz, Madeira

name: Capela de São Pedro Gonçalves Telmo
summary: The Capela de São Pedro Gonçalves Telmo was a former chapel near the beach at Calheta. The Elucidário refers the reader to the entry Corpo Santo.
location: near the beach, parish and municipality of Calheta

name: Ponte da Fonte da Areia.
summary: The Ponta da Fonte da Areia is a small point on the north-west coast of Porto Santo, at Fonte da Areia.
location: Fonte da Areia, north-west coast of Porto Santo

name: Fonte da Areia
summary: Fonte da Areia is a locality on the north coast of Porto Santo. It has a drinking fountain and is a popular excursion spot.
location: north coast of Porto Santo

name: Pico da Fonte da Bica
summary: The Pico da Fonte da Bica is a peak of 1,560 metres on the Paul da Serra plateau, Madeira.
location: Paul da Serra plateau, Madeira

name: Fonte dos Ingleses
summary: Fonte dos Ingleses is a pleasant spot with a clear spring at Fanal, in the uplands of the parish of Ribeira da Janela, Madeira.
location: Fanal, in the uplands of the parish of Ribeira da Janela, Madeira

name: Fonte Vermelha
summary: Fonte Vermelha is a roadside spot in the parish of Santo António, Funchal, on the road from Santo António to Curral das Freiras. A drinking fountain was built there in 1847.
location: on the road from Santo António to Curral das Freiras, parish of Santo António, municipality of Funchal

name: Tábua
summary: Tábua is a parish in the municipality of Ribeira Brava, Madeira. The Elucidário covers the origin of its name, its creation and clergy stipends, its parish church and chapels, its early settlers and its principal localities.
location: parish in the municipality of Ribeira Brava, Madeira

name: Capelas de Nossa Senhora da Vida
summary: These are two chapels dedicated to Nossa Senhora da Vida in the Funchal area. One was founded by Manuel Valente in 1679 in the parish of São Pedro, though its site is unknown; the other was founded by Inês Teixeira at Fajã do Mar.
location: municipality of Funchal (one in São Pedro parish; another at Fajã do Mar)

name: Capela de Nossa Senhora das Vitórias
summary: The Capela de Nossa Senhora das Vitórias is a former chapel in Machico, built in 1749.
location: Machico, Madeira

name: Capela de Nosso Senhor Jesus Cristo
summary: The Capela de Nosso Senhor Jesus Cristo is a fifteenth-century chapel in Santa Cruz founded by Gil Anes. It later became the seat of an entailed estate.
location: Santa Cruz, Madeira

name: Nova de Santa Maria
summary: Rua Nova de Santa Maria is a street in Funchal, opened after the 1803 flood and running parallel to Rua de Santa Maria. It is now named Latino Coelho.
location: Funchal, parallel to Rua de Santa Maria

name: Nova Aldeia ou Aldeia da Rainha
aliases: Nova Aldeia ou Aldeia da Rainha
summary: Nova Aldeia, or Aldeia da Rainha, was a short-lived settlement at Santo da Serra. It was founded by royal charter in 1768 for families moved there from Porto Santo.
location: Santo da Serra, Madeira

name: Ribeira dos Moinhos
summary: Ribeira dos Moinhos is a small stream in Madeira that rises on the Pico da Fonte do Barro.
location: rises on the Pico da Fonte do Barro, Madeira

name: Ribeira da Cruz
summary: Ribeira da Cruz is a small stream in Madeira that rises on the Pico da Pedreira.
location: rises on the Pico da Pedreira, Madeira

name: Ribeira da Janela
summary: The Ribeira da Janela is one of the longest and fullest streams of Madeira. It rises in the Paul da Serra, the Rabaçal springs and Assobiadouro.
location: rises in the Paul da Serra, Rabaçal and Assobiadouro, Madeira

name: Vicente
summary: The São Vicente stream in Madeira rises on the Ferreiros and Cumeada peaks. It is fed by the Ribeira Grande and the Atalho brook.
location: São Vicente, Madeira

name: Ribeira dos Moinhos
summary: This Ribeira dos Moinhos is a stream that rises in the Serra da Boaventura. It is shorter than the Ribeira do Porco.
location: Serra da Boaventura, parish of Boaventura, Madeira

name: Ribeira da Boaventura
summary: The Ribeira da Boaventura is one of the fullest streams of Madeira. It rises at Boca das Torrinhas and is called the Ribeira do Porco near the village.
location: rises at Boca das Torrinhas, Boaventura, Madeira

name: Jorge
summary: The São Jorge stream in Madeira rises on the Pico do Canário. It is fed by the Canário, Grande and Tombo da Furna brooks.
location: São Jorge, Madeira

name: Ribeira do Faial
summary: The Ribeira do Faial, also called the Ribeira Seca, is a stream in Madeira that rises on Pico Ruivo. It is fed by the Ribeira da Metade and the Ribeiro Frio.
location: rises on Pico Ruivo, Faial, Madeira

name: Beco do Ribeirinho
summary: The Beco do Ribeirinho is an alley in Funchal linking the Travessa do Rego and the Travessa da Conveniência. In 1902 the council allowed part of it to be closed off.
location: Funchal, between the Travessa do Rego and the Travessa da Conveniência

name: Rua do Ribeirinho
summary: Rua do Ribeirinho is the former name of a Funchal street, taken from the Vale brook. It was later called Rua das Hortas and is now Rua do Alferes Veiga Pestana.
location: Funchal

name: Nossa Senhora do Monte
summary: Nossa Senhora do Monte, commonly called Monte, is a parish above Funchal. The Elucidário covers its origin in Adão Gonçalves Ferreira's chapel, the legend of the Virgin's apparition, the building of the church and the island-wide cult and August pilgrimage. It also covers the parish's quintas, railway and toboggans.
location: parish above Funchal, municipality of Funchal

name: Porto e Cais da Ribeira Brava
summary: This is the landing place of Ribeira Brava, a pebble beach where embarking was difficult. A quay was built there between 1904 and 1908, linked to the town by a tunnel and a short road and served by coastal steamers.
location: Ribeira Brava, parish and municipality of Ribeira Brava

name: Capelas de Nossa Senhora do Amparo
summary: These are several chapels in Madeira dedicated to Our Lady of Amparo. The chief one is at Álamos (Água de Mel) in Santo António, seat of the Água de Mel entail; others stood in São Martinho, Ponta do Pargo and Machico.
location: Álamos (Água de Mel), parish of Santo António, municipality of Funchal (principal chapel)

name: Capelas de Nossa Senhora da Boa Viagem
aliases: Nossa Senhora da Boa Viagem (Capelas de)
summary: These are two chapels of Our Lady of Good Voyage in Funchal. One was founded in 1711 at Carne Azeda in Santa Luzia. The other is an ancient chapel in Santa Maria Maior founded by Bento da Veiga, whose adjoining house reputedly held the first customs house.
location: Carne Azeda, parish of Santa Luzia, and parish of Santa Maria Maior, municipality of Funchal

name: Capela de Nossa Senhora do Bom Despacho
aliases: Nossa Senhora do Bom Despacho (Capela de)
summary: This is a chapel in Campanário founded in 1672 by the morgado Jerónimo de Atouguia Bettencourt and his wife. It was rebuilt in 1762 and still belonged to the Brito family in 1921.
location: Campanário, municipality of Ribeira Brava

name: Capelas de Nossa Senhora do Bom Sucesso
aliases: Nossa Senhora do Bom Sucesso (Capelas de)
summary: These are three chapels of Our Lady of Good Success. One is at Garachico, straddling the boundary of Câmara de Lobos and Estreito de Câmara de Lobos; another is at Lombo da Estrela in Calheta (1683). The third, on the Caminho do Meio in Funchal, is owned by the municipal council.
location: Garachico, on the boundary of Câmara de Lobos and Estreito de Câmara de Lobos parishes, municipality of Câmara de Lobos (principal chapel)

name: Visconde do Ribeiro Rea
summary: Visconde do Ribeiro Rea is a square in Funchal by the Rua da Carreira, where the bishop's palace has its main entrance. It occupies the site of the old British cemetery, demolished in 1888.
location: Funchal, by the Rua da Carreira

name: São Jorge
summary: São Jorge is a parish on Madeira's north coast, in the municipality of Santana. The Elucidário records its early settlement and land grants, the creation of the parish in the mid-sixteenth century, and its eighteenth-century church with notable gilded woodwork and sculpture. It also lists the parish's main localities and its population in 1921.
location: parish in the municipality of Santana, north coast of Madeira

name: Passos
summary: The Passos were oratories of the Stations of the Passion that stood in the streets of Funchal. The Procession of the Passos halted at each of them.
location: streets of Funchal, Madeira

name: Asilos
summary: Asilos refers to the first attempt by the Funchal Municipal Council, made before constitutional government, to found a charitable home for orphans and invalids. The attempt was unsuccessful.
location: Funchal, Madeira

name: Cais na Ilha do Porto Santo
aliases: Cais na Ilha do Porto Santo
summary: The entry records the pier serving the island of Porto Santo. It also notes a plan of 1824 for a mole and quay at the Baixas de São Tiago in Funchal, which was abandoned.

name: Castanho
summary: Pico do Castanho is a peak 628 m high on the northern coast of the parish of Caniçal, in the municipality of Machico.
location: northern coast of the parish of Caniçal, municipality of Machico

name: Castanho
summary: Pico do Castanho is a hill with wide views in the parish of Machico. Rebel and government troops clashed on its slopes on 2 May 1931.
location: parish of Machico, municipality of Machico

name: Boca das Torrinhas
summary: Boca das Torrinhas is a mountain pass separating the serra of Boaventura from that of Curral das Freiras. The Elucidário notes it for the plants Sedum farinosum and Isoplexis sceptrum.
location: mountain pass between the serras of Boaventura and Curral das Freiras

name: Bôca das Voltas
summary: Bôca das Voltas is a site at about 750 m between Pico do Arco and Pico do Canário. It is the starting point of a path down to the Ribeira da Boaventura.
location: between Pico do Arco and Pico do Canário, parish of Boaventura

name: Boca do Buraco
summary: Boca do Buraco is a viewpoint east of Pico do Areeiro. It offers a fine panorama on clear days.
location: east of Pico do Areeiro, Madeira

name: Boca dos Corregos
summary: Boca dos Corregos is a site at about 1300 m near Pico Grande. It overlooks Curral das Freiras and the Serra de Água valley.
location: near Pico Grande, Madeira

name: Pico dos Bodes
summary: Pico dos Bodes is a peak of about 1135 m near Boca dos Namorados, in the parish of Estreito de Câmara de Lobos.
location: parish of Estreito de Câmara de Lobos, municipality of Câmara de Lobos

name: Pico dos Bodes
summary: This Pico dos Bodes is an elevation of 1300 m in the serra of Ribeira da Janela. It shares its name with a peak in Estreito de Câmara de Lobos.
location: serra of Ribeira da Janela, Madeira

name: Machico
summary: Machico is a town and municipality of Madeira set in a valley. The Elucidário traces its municipal history from its probable creation around 1451, through the loss of territory to Santa Cruz, São Vicente and Santana. It also records its arms, its privileges and its new town hall of 1929.
location: town and municipality of Machico, Madeira

name: Santo António
summary: Santo António is the most populous suburban parish of Funchal, which originated as a curacy around 1557. The Elucidário covers its clergy stipends and the building of its parish churches. It also covers its chapels, its sítios and later improvements.
location: suburban parish of the municipality of Funchal

name: Túmulo-Monumento
summary: The Túmulo-Monumento is a memorial in the Angústias cemetery in Funchal. It commemorates those killed by German submarine shells at Funchal on 3 December 1916 and was handed to the municipal council in 1917.
location: Angústias cemetery, Funchal

name: Túmulos
summary: The Elucidário notes that Madeiran churches contain few notable tombs. It cites the Brandão family mausoleums in the Carmo church and the tomb in Santa Clara said to hold Zargo.
location: Funchal, Madeira

name: Quintas
summary: In Madeira a 'quinta' is a walled country or suburban estate with a fine house and gardens, often with farmland and a chapel. The Elucidário explains this meaning and lists the island's most notable quintas and their owners.

name: São Roque
summary: São Roque is a suburban parish of Funchal, separated from São Pedro and created under a royal charter of 1579; it is named after its original chapel of São Roque. The Elucidário traces the history of its parish church and lists its chapels, principal localities and population.
location: suburban parish of the municipality of Funchal

name: Águas de São Roque
summary: The Águas de São Roque are a cold spring at Machico, long reputed for their therapeutic virtues. Charles Lepierre's analysis of 1896 classed the water as hypothermal, hyposaline and sodium-chloride, and found it free of coliform bacteria.
location: Machico, municipality of Machico

name: Necrotério
summary: The Necrotério is the mortuary at the Angústias cemetery in Funchal. It was built by order of the municipal council in 1900 to hold the bodies of the poor and the unclaimed.
location: Angústias cemetery, Funchal

name: Travessa do Nery
summary: The Travessa do Nery was a lane in the parish of Santa Maria Maior, Funchal, named after Canon Vicente Nery da Silva. It was later widened and renamed Caminho do Acciaioly.
location: parish of Santa Maria Maior, Funchal

name: Baixa do Galeão
summary: The Baixa do Galeão is a reef or shoal lying east of the harbour of São Vicente, not far from the coast.
location: east of the harbour of São Vicente, municipality of São Vicente

name: Capela de São João e Santana
summary: The Capela de São João e Santana is a chapel built in 1814 by João António de Gouveia Rego at the Quinta do Trapiche in Santo António, Funchal. The house adjoining it later housed the seminary.
location: Quinta do Trapiche, parish of Santo António, municipality of Funchal

name: Capela de Nossa Senhora do Pilar
summary: The Capela de Nossa Senhora do Pilar is a private chapel with a quinta at the Pilar site in São Martinho, Funchal. It was founded in 1676 by Gonçalo de Freitas Drumond.
location: sítio of Pilar, parish of São Martinho, municipality of Funchal

name: Capelas de Nossa Senhora dos Prazeres
summary: Two chapels were dedicated to Nossa Senhora dos Prazeres. One was founded in 1611 by Tristão Gomes de Castro in Monte (later Santa Luzia); the other was an entailed chapel in Santa Maria Maior.
location: Monte (later Santa Luzia) and Santa Maria Maior, Funchal

name: Capelas de Nossa Senhora das Preces
summary: Collective entry on three chapels dedicated to Nossa Senhora das Preces, at Santo António (c.1708), Câmara de Lobos (1683) and Machico. Each chapel gives its name to the surrounding site.
location: Santo António, Câmara de Lobos and Machico, Madeira

name: Capela de Nossa Senhora dos Remédios e Amparo
aliases: Nossa Senhora dos Remédios e Amparo (Capela de)
summary: A chapel attached to the manor house of the viscounts of São João on Rua das Maravilhas, Funchal. It was built by Dr. Rui Bettencourt da Câmara and blessed on 1 January 1940.
location: Rua das Maravilhas, Funchal, Madeira

name: Ponta do Pargo
summary: Parish at the western tip of Madeira's south coast, in the municipality of Calheta, named after a huge pargo fish caught there during the discovery voyage. It was created from Fajã da Ovelha. The Elucidário covers its church, schools, entailed estates, farming, levadas, lighthouse and administrative history.
location: parish in the municipality of Calheta, western tip of Madeira

name: Alagoas
summary: A small plateau in the Serra do Poiso, Madeira, close to the shelter house there.
location: Serra do Poiso, Madeira

name: Convento da Incarnaçao
summary: The Convent of Nossa Senhora da Incarnação in Funchal was founded in 1650 by Canon Henrique Calaça de Viveiros to celebrate Portugal's restoration of independence. Its site was later used as a British barracks, the diocesan seminary and offices of the Junta Geral.
location: Funchal, Madeira

name: Pico da Fajã da Ovelha
summary: A mountain peak in the uplands of the parish of Fajã da Ovelha, Madeira, not far from the Pico da Fonte do Bispo.
location: uplands of the parish of Fajã da Ovelha, Madeira

name: Ponta da Fajã da Ovelha
summary: A headland on the coast of the parish of Fajã da Ovelha, Madeira.
location: coast of the parish of Fajã da Ovelha, Madeira

name: Fajã das Nogueiras
summary: A locality in the uplands of Faial parish, Madeira, with a small shelter house for travellers.
location: uplands of the parish of Faial, Madeira

name: Fajã do Mar
summary: An inhabited locality in Arco da Calheta, Madeira. It has the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Vida, founded in 1663 by Inez Teixeira.
location: sítio in the parish of Arco da Calheta, municipality of Calheta

name: Livramento
summary: Inhabited locality in the parish of Caniço, Madeira, named after a former chapel of Nossa Senhora do Livramento. The chapel's popular pilgrimage has moved to the parish church.
location: sítio in the parish of Caniço, Madeira

name: Livramento
summary: Inhabited locality in the parish of Monte, Funchal, named after its entailed chapel of Nossa Senhora do Livramento (1684). It also has a recent chapel of the Sacred Heart.
location: sítio in the parish of Monte, municipality of Funchal

name: Livramento
summary: Locality in Ponta do Sol parish, Madeira. It has a chapel of Nossa Senhora do Livramento, built in 1656 as the seat of an entail.
location: sítio in the parish of Ponta do Sol, municipality of Ponta do Sol

name: Livramento
summary: Locality in São Vicente parish, Madeira, named after its chapel of Nossa Senhora do Livramento, founded in 1683.
location: sítio in the parish of São Vicente, municipality of São Vicente

name: Ribeira Brava
summary: Municipality of Madeira created in 1914 from parishes of Ponta do Sol and Câmara de Lobos. Its seat, the sítio of Lugar, was raised to the status of vila in 1928.
location: municipality of Ribeira Brava, Madeira

name: Populaçâo, Superficie e Situaçâo Geográfica da ilha do Porto Santo
aliases: Porto Santo (Populaçâo, Superficie e Situaçâo Geográfica da ilha do)
summary: Statistical entry on the island of Porto Santo. It gives the island's population from 1529 to 1940, the differing estimates of its surface area, and its geographical coordinates.
location: island of Porto Santo

name: Fontes de João Diniz
summary: Springs beside the São Lourenço fortress in Funchal, long used as a public water source by townspeople and ships. They disappeared in November 1939 during repairs to the palace.
location: beside the São Lourenço fortress, Funchal, Madeira

name: Edifícios Antigos
summary: Survey of the oldest surviving civil and religious buildings of Madeira. It deals especially with Funchal houses with Gothic twin-light windows, most since demolished, and with the churches Dr Neale described as late Gothic in 1844.

name: Lazareto
summary: The quarantine station (lazaretto) of Funchal. Plans in 1816 went unrealised and temporary sites were used before buildings were erected at the mouth of the Ribeira de Gonçalo Aires (1866–74). These were later used during epidemics and to hold political prisoners.
location: mouth of the Ribeira de Gonçalo Aires, Funchal, Madeira

name: Capelas de Nossa Senhora da Nazaré
summary: Collective entry on three Madeiran chapels dedicated to Nossa Senhora da Nazaré, in Arco da Calheta, Câmara de Lobos and São Martinho. It gives their founders and dates, and a fishermen's tradition about the lady of the entail at Câmara de Lobos.
location: Arco da Calheta, Câmara de Lobos and São Martinho, Madeira

name: Pontas
summary: List of the principal headlands (pontas) of Madeira, Porto Santo and the Desertas, grouped by municipality.

name: Fortaleza do Pico
summary: Former fortification on the Pico do Castelo in Porto Santo, built under Philippine rule after the Moorish raid of 1617. It served as a refuge from pirates rather than as a true stronghold.
location: Pico do Castelo, Porto Santo

name: Pico dos Barcelos
summary: A hill and viewpoint in Santo António parish overlooking Funchal. A commemorative cross was inaugurated there in 1941.
location: parish of Santo António, municipality of Funchal

name: Funchal Antigo
summary: Reconstruction of the layout of Funchal in 1508, when the town was raised to city status. It describes which streets, churches, chapels, convents and other buildings already existed and which came later.
location: Funchal, Madeira

name: Casas de Abrigo
summary: Mountain refuge huts built in the high serras of Madeira to shelter travellers caught by storms. The Elucidário lists those existing at the time and notes their poor state and staffing.
location: high serras of Madeira

name: Manicómios
summary: History of provision for the mentally ill in Madeira, beginning with a 1493 request for a 'Tronco'. It records the founding of the Manicómio Câmara Pestana at the Quinta do Rochedo (1906) and of the Casa de Saúde de São João de Deus at the Trapiche (1922–24).

name: Aspectos Hidrográficos: Baias, Enseadas, Portos e Praias da Madeira
aliases: Madeira (Aspectos Hidrográficos: Baias, Enseadas, Portos e Praias da)
summary: Survey entry on the coastline of Madeira. It describes the two bays (Funchal and Porto Santo), the small coves, the landing places graded as good, fair or poor, and the island's mostly pebble beaches. It serves as an index to the individual entries on each port and beach.
location: Coast of Madeira and Porto Santo

name: Ponta do Sol
aliases: Ponta do Sol (Vila e Município da)
summary: Town and municipality of Ponta do Sol on Madeira, an early sugar-producing centre raised to a town in 1501. The Elucidário traces the changes in its municipal territory and its role as seat of a judicial district (comarca).
location: Town and municipality of Ponta do Sol, Madeira

name: Amparo
summary: Locality in the parish of São Martinho, Funchal. It has the chapel of Nossa Senhora do Amparo, founded in 1712 by D. Luísa de Mendonça and belonging to the Sauvaire entail.
location: Sítio in the parish of São Martinho, municipality of Funchal

name: Amparo
summary: Locality in the parish of Ponta do Pargo, named after its chapel of Nossa Senhora do Amparo. The chapel's feast draws people from neighbouring parishes.
location: Sítio in the parish of Ponta do Pargo, municipality of Calheta

name: Desertas
summary: The main headlands of the Desertas group: Ponta de Santa Maria, Castanheira, Pedregal and Ponta das Agulhas.
location: Desertas Islands

name: Porto Santo
summary: Survey entry on the coastal and water features of Porto Santo. It covers the great southern bay and beach, minor landing places, shoals, islets, the raised fossil beach and the island's small seasonal streams.
location: Island and municipality of Porto Santo

name: Águas Doces
summary: A small beach and stretch of coast near Funchal, lying between the Ilhéu da Pontinha and the mouth of the Ribeiro Seco.
location: Coast near Funchal, between the Ilhéu da Pontinha and the mouth of the Ribeiro Seco

name: Águas férreas
summary: Entry on Madeira's iron-bearing springs. The chief of these is the Jamboto spring in Santo António, analysed by Carlos Lepierre in 1900.
location: Jamboto, parish of Santo António, municipality of Funchal

name: Capelas de São José
summary: Survey of chapels dedicated to Saint Joseph in Madeira and Porto Santo, with their founders and dates. It covers chapels in Ribeira Brava, Calheta, Porto Santo, Machico, Santa Cruz and Camacha.

name: Praça do Município
summary: Square in Funchal, formerly the Largo do Colégio. It was created in 1836 on part of the churchyard of São João Evangelista and greatly enlarged in 1943–44.
location: Square in the city of Funchal

name: Farol do Porto Santo
summary: Lighthouse on the Ilhéu de Cima off Porto Santo. It began operating in 1901, forty years after the São Lourenço light, after coastal shipwrecks had shown the need for it.
location: Ilhéu de Cima, off Porto Santo

name: Farol da Ponta do Pargo
summary: Lighthouse at Ponta do Pargo, at the western end of Madeira's south coast. It was built before the First World War but only inaugurated on 5 June 1922.
location: Ponta do Pargo, western end of Madeira's south coast

name: Fortificações
summary: Survey of the history of Madeira's coastal fortifications, from the first requests for a fortress at Funchal in the fifteenth century to anti-submarine batteries built in 1916–17. It lists the forts, redoubts and batteries built in each period across Madeira and Porto Santo.

name: Furna da Mulher
summary: A cave or sea grotto on the western coast of Deserta Grande in the Desertas Islands.
location: Western coast of Deserta Grande, Desertas Islands

name: Ponta da Água
summary: Coastal point in Câmara de Lobos parish near Cabo Girão, midway between Fajã das Pedras and Fajã dos Asnos.
location: Coast of the parish and municipality of Câmara de Lobos, near Cabo Girão, between Fajã das Pedras and Fajã dos Asnos

name: Cadeia
summary: The prison of the Funchal judicial district. It was first in an old house on the Rua da Cadeia Velha, then for nearly a century in a building on the Largo da Sé, and from 1913 in a new prison built on the site of the São Lázaro hospital.
location: Funchal

name: Capela de Nossa Senhora de Belém
summary: Extinct chapel of Our Lady of Bethlehem at Câmara de Lobos, founded in 1649 and rebuilt in 1758. The entry also notes a chapel of the same name at Porto da Cruz.
location: Parish and municipality of Câmara de Lobos

name: Capelas de Nossa Senhora da Boa Hora
aliases: Nossa Senhora da Boa Hora (Capelas de)
summary: Entry on the chapels of Our Lady of Boa Hora. These stand at Torre (Câmara de Lobos), above Funchal (1726) and at Fajã in Arco da Calheta.

name: Capela de Nossa Senhora da Boa Nova
aliases: Nossa Senhora da Boa Nova (Capela de)
summary: Chapel of Our Lady of Boa Nova in São Gonçalo parish, Funchal, founded in 1701.
location: Parish of São Gonçalo, municipality of Funchal

name: Santana
summary: Municipality on Madeira's north coast, created in 1835. It lost Porto da Cruz to Machico in 1852 and was briefly abolished in 1867.
location: Municipality of Santana, north coast of Madeira

name: Santa Apolónia
summary: A small ruined chapel of Santa Apolónia in Calheta. It belonged to the former Franciscan convent there.
location: Parish and municipality of Calheta

name: Capela de Santa Brigida
summary: A lost chapel of Santa Brígida in São Pedro parish, Funchal, founded in 1668. Its site is unknown.
location: Parish of São Pedro, municipality of Funchal

name: Boaventura
summary: Parish on the north coast of Madeira, in the municipality of São Vicente, separated from Ponta Delgada in 1836. The Elucidário covers its obscure name, church history, levadas, localities and a local anecdote about General Beresford.
location: Parish of Boaventura, municipality of São Vicente

name: Capelas de São Paulo
summary: Entry on the chapels dedicated to Saint Paul in Madeira. Chief among them is the ancient chapel on the Largo de São Paulo in Funchal, founded by João Gonçalves Zarco, which briefly housed the parish of São Pedro; there is also a ruined chapel at Porto Moniz.
location: Largo de São Paulo, parish of São Pedro, Funchal

name: Porto e Cais do Campanario
summary: A small, poor landing place on the coast of Campanário parish. A modest landing stage was built there in 1909.
location: Coast of the parish of Campanário

name: Carlos
summary: Campo de D. Carlos was a square in Funchal, built between 1898 and 1901 to improve the Santa Maria Maior area and named after King Carlos. It was renamed Campo do Almirante Reis in 1911.
location: Santa Maria Maior, Funchal

name: Capelas de São Luís
summary: The Elucidário records two chapels dedicated to São Luís. One is an early eighteenth-century chapel at Diferença in Faial. The other was built by Bishop D. Luís Figueiredo de Lemos beside the old Episcopal Palace in Funchal, and he was buried there.
location: Diferença, parish of Faial; and beside the old Episcopal Palace, Funchal

name: Preces
summary: Preces is a locality in the parish of Machico, within the inhabited sítio of Marco. It is named after the chapel of Nossa Senhora das Preces, founded in 1750.
location: within the sítio of Marco, parish and municipality of Machico

name: Preces
summary: Preces is an inhabited locality in the parish of Santo António, Funchal. It has a chapel of Nossa Senhora das Preces built in 1768.
location: locality in the parish of Santo António, municipality of Funchal

name: Preces
summary: Preces, also called Caminho Grande, is a sítio in the parish of Câmara de Lobos. It has the chapels of Nossa Senhora das Preces (1683) and Nossa Senhora da Nazaré (1757), and the ruins of a chapel of São Cândido.
location: sítio in the parish and municipality of Câmara de Lobos

name: Norte da Ilha
summary: 'Norte da Ilha' is the common name for Madeira's northern coast, from Ponta do Tristão to Ponta de São Lourenço. It covers the municipalities of Porto Moniz, São Vicente and Santana and the parish of Porto da Cruz.
location: northern coast of Madeira, from Ponta do Tristão to Ponta de São Lourenço

name: Posto Marítimo de Desinfecção
summary: The Posto Marítimo de Desinfecção is a small maritime disinfection station that has operated at the Pontinha in Funchal since 1901. It was funded through the Junta Geral and staffed by government-paid personnel.
location: Pontinha, Funchal

name: Posto Médico Municipal
summary: The Posto Médico Municipal is the municipal medical post of Funchal, opened by the town council in 1889. It acquired an X-ray apparatus in 1922.
location: Funchal

name: Porto e cais da Oliveira
summary: The Porto e cais da Oliveira is a small quay at Ponta da Oliveira in Caniço, built in 1909. It is linked to the main road by a branch 1,800 metres long.
location: Ponta da Oliveira, parish of Caniço

name: Porto e Praia do Arco de São Jorge
aliases: Arco de São Jorge (Porto e Praia do)
summary: The Porto e Praia do Arco de São Jorge is a small, poor landing place with a short beach on the coast of the parish of Arco de São Jorge. Disembarking there is difficult.
location: coast of the parish of Arco de São Jorge

name: Cais
summary: This general entry introduces Madeira's twenty-six quays, most of them built or improved by the Junta Geral between 1905 and 1916. They made coastal landings and communication between parishes easier.

name: Órgão de Santa Clara
summary: The Órgão de Santa Clara is the old organ of the extinct Convent of Santa Clara in Funchal, said to have been given by the children of João Gonçalves Zarco in 1498. The Elucidário reproduces a 1924 newspaper article on its restoration, which also mentions the similar restoration of the organ of Machico parish church.
location: former Convent of Santa Clara, Funchal

name: Moradias de Zargo
summary: The Moradias de Zargo are the successive residences of João Gonçalves Zargo in Funchal: a wooden house by the Santa Catarina chapel, a stone house near São Paulo, and a final home near the Conceição de Cima (Santa Clara) church. The author identifies this last house with the present Quinta das Cruzes, and the entry traces its later owners and the two-handed sword attributed to Zargo.
location: Funchal (final residence near the Conceição de Cima/Santa Clara church, identified with the Quinta das Cruzes)

name: Conceição
summary: Conceição is a locality in the parish of Estreito da Calheta with a chapel of Nossa Senhora da Conceição built in 1673. It was once the seat of one of Madeira's largest entailed estates.
location: locality in the parish of Estreito da Calheta, municipality of Calheta

name: Conceição
summary: Conceição is a locality in Ribeira Brava named after its chapel of the Conceição. The chapel's founder and date are unknown.
location: locality in the municipality of Ribeira Brava

name: Conceição
summary: Conceição is an inhabited locality in São Roque, Funchal. It has a chapel of Nossa Senhora da Conceição built in 1700.
location: locality in São Roque, municipality of Funchal

name: Baixa da Conceição.
summary: The Baixa da Conceição is a shoal near the Ilhéu da Lapa off the coast of Campanário.
location: off the coast of the parish of Campanário, near the Ilhéu da Lapa

name: Largo da Conceição
summary: The Largo da Conceição is a square in Funchal, commonly called Largo das Babosas. It is named after the Capela-Monumento of the Conceição, built in 1906 to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the dogma.
location: Funchal

name: Ruivo
summary: Pico Ruivo is the highest peak of Madeira, at the southern edge of Santana parish; the 1914 geodetic survey gave its height as 1,861 m. The Elucidário describes the routes to the summit, earlier height measurements, its panorama, vegetation and geology, and the shelter built there in 1939.
location: southern edge of the parish of Santana, municipality of Santana

name: Porto e Ribeira de São Vicente
summary: The Porto e Ribeira de São Vicente comprises the small, difficult landing place at São Vicente on Madeira's north coast and the São Vicente stream. At the stream's mouth stands a chapel on a basalt rock, and there is a lava cave nearby.
location: parish and municipality of São Vicente, north coast of Madeira

name: Capelas de São Francisco
summary: The Elucidário gives notes on three chapels dedicated to St Francis: in Calheta, in São Pedro (São Francisco das Furnas) and in Santa Luzia.
location: Calheta; São Pedro (Funchal); Santa Luzia

name: Capela de Sao Francisco de Borja
summary: The Capela de São Francisco de Borja is a chapel of St Francis Borgia built in 1760 by D. Francisco de Vasconcelos at Cruz da Guarda, Porto da Cruz. The Elucidário corrects the 'Saudades', which attributed it to St Francis Xavier.
location: Cruz da Guarda, parish of Porto da Cruz, municipality of Machico

name: Capelas de São Francisco Xavier
summary: The Elucidário records chapels of St Francis Xavier in Calheta (1693), Santa Cruz (1684) and Porto da Cruz.
location: Calheta; Santa Cruz; Porto da Cruz

name: Hermenegildo Capelo
summary: Rua Hermenegildo Capelo is a street in Funchal beside the Jardim Municipal. It was opened in 1814 through the grounds of the former Franciscan convent and renamed in 1885 after the explorer Hermenegildo Capelo.
location: beside the Jardim Municipal, Funchal

name: Rua do Chapéu
summary: Rua do Chapéu is the former name of a stretch of the present Rua Correia Heredia in Funchal, between Rua da Figueira Preta and Rua do Bom Jesus.
location: Rua Correia Heredia, between Rua da Figueira Preta and Rua do Bom Jesus, Funchal

name: Chaves
summary: Rua do Dr. Chaves is a street in Funchal, formerly called Rua dos Aranhas. It is named after Dr Chaves, a graduate of the Funchal medical-surgical school and a member of the town council.
location: Street in Funchal

name: Enseada e Porto do Lugar de Baixo
aliases: Lugar de Baixo (Enseada e Porto do)
summary: A small cove and beach landing place at Lugar de Baixo. It was sometimes better for landing than the quays of Ponta do Sol and Ribeira Brava. Infante D. Luís landed there in 1858.
location: Lugar de Baixo, parish and municipality of Ponta do Sol, Madeira

name: Capela de Nossa Senhora do Carmo
summary: A chapel of Our Lady of Mount Carmel, built in 1658 by the merchant Domingos Rodrigues on his estate in Campanário.
location: Campanário, Madeira

name: Igreja de Nossa Senhora do Carmo
summary: The Carmo church in Funchal was built in 1656–1660 for the Third Order of Carmel and gave its name to its street. It contains the only artistically notable mausoleums on the island.
location: Funchal

name: Ferreiros
summary: Rua dos Ferreiros is one of Funchal's busiest streets, running from Rua 5 de Outubro to the Torreão bridge. It was earlier known by the names Peru, Estudo and Pinheiro, and was renamed Rua do Comércio in 1915.
location: Street in Funchal, between Rua 5 de Outubro and the Torreão bridge

name: Baixo
summary: Pico de Baixo is a hill in the northern part of Porto Santo island, lying towards the east-south-east.
location: Northern part of Porto Santo, towards the east-south-east

name: Arquipélago da Madeira
summary: The Madeira archipelago, which forms the administrative district of Funchal. The Elucidário surveys its historical and scientific importance, geographical position, extreme points, coordinates, area and population.

name: Calhau e Porto da Aldonça
summary: A small landing place with a short beach on the coast of Gaula parish.
location: Coast of the parish of Gaula, Madeira

name: Primitivas Habitações
summary: This entry describes the earliest dwellings built in Madeira after its discovery, which were made of timber from the native forests. It also records traditions about the first two-storey house and the first stone houses in Funchal.

name: Capelas de Santo António
summary: A survey of the chapels dedicated to Saint Anthony across Madeira, from the 16th to the early 20th century. For each chapel it gives the parish, founder, date of construction or blessing and later fate, whether surviving, rebuilt or vanished.

name: Madeira
aliases: Madeira (Aspectos orográficos: Encostas, Planaltos e Vales)
summary: A survey of Madeira's relief, covering the central east–west mountain range and its peaks, the few plateaux, the main coastal headlands and the principal valleys. It also explains the traditional division of the island into a North Coast and a South Coast.
location: Island of Madeira

name: Faróis
summary: A brief account of early attempts to light the coasts of Madeira. It notes in particular an unsuccessful parliamentary bill of 1861 for lighthouses at Ponta de São Lourenço and on the Pontinha islet.

name: Farolim do Ilhéu
summary: A small fixed-light beacon on the islet at Funchal harbour, popularly known as 'a brasa do ilhéu'. It was in service from 1866 until it was replaced in 1931.
location: Islet at Funchal harbour

name: Sé Catedral
summary: Funchal Cathedral is a Gothic-Manueline national monument, begun in the 1490s under D. Manuel and consecrated in 1516. The Elucidário covers its construction history and architecture, including its Mudéjar cedar ceiling, chapels, processional cross and organs.
location: Funchal

name: Porto do Porto do Moniz
summary: The harbour of Porto do Moniz is reputedly the safest and most sheltered anchorage on Madeira's north coast, used as a refuge when southerly winds close the southern ports. The Elucidário records hydrographic studies made in 1914 and harbour works carried out between 1901 and 1916.
location: Porto do Moniz, parish and municipality of Porto Moniz, north coast of Madeira

name: Fajãzinha de Bento
summary: A locality in the parish of Serra de Água where Funchal Municipal Council owned a small property, which was sold in 1918.
location: Locality in the parish of Serra de Água, Madeira

name: Machico
summary: The parish of Machico was the landing place of the discoverers Zargo and Tristão Vaz and the seat of the captaincy of Machico; the parish was founded c. 1450. The Elucidário covers its clergy and stipends, chapels, historical events, mineral springs, localities, population and notable natives.
location: Parish of Machico, municipality of Machico, Madeira

name: Baixa, Enseada e Porto dos Barbeiros
summary: The Barbeiros shoal, the Enseada dos Barbeiros (also called Enseada de Guilherme) and a small landing place of the same name, on the coast of Porto Santo.
location: Porto Santo, between the Ponta da Cruz and the Ponta do Ninho do Guincho

name: Ponta Delgada
summary: Ponta Delgada is a parish on Madeira's north coast. The Elucidário covers the origin of its name, the church of Senhor Bom Jesus and its ancient pilgrimage, its clergy, notable residents, agriculture and services.
location: Parish of Ponta Delgada, municipality of São Vicente, north coast of Madeira

name: Ribeira da Janela
summary: The Ribeira da Janela is the longest and fullest stream in Madeira. It rises on the Paul da Serra and feeds the Rabaçal levadas.
location: Rises on the Paul da Serra; parish of Ribeira da Janela, municipality of Porto Moniz, Madeira

name: Muncipio do Porto do Moniz
summary: The municipality of Porto Moniz in north-western Madeira was created in 1835 after long local petitions and was repeatedly abolished and restored in the nineteenth century. Porto Moniz was never raised to the status of a vila, serving only as the seat of the concelho.
location: North-western Madeira

name: Casa de Saúde
summary: A small former building at the Entrada da Cidade in Funchal, first used by the health guards who inspected arriving ships. It later served as the town hall and as the seat of the Port Captaincy and the Commercial Association, and was sold by the council in 1914.
location: Entrada da Cidade, Funchal

name: Casa dos Consules
summary: An 18th-century town house in Funchal, named after the consulates once housed there. It is admired for its architecture.
location: Corner of Rua da Conceição and Rua da Figueira Preta, Funchal

name: Funchal – I Origem do nome
summary: The first part of the Elucidário's entry on Funchal, whose name derives from the fennel plant (funcho). It records the creation of the town and municipality around 1451–52 and its elevation to city status by King Manuel I in 1508, transcribing the royal charter in full.
location: Funchal, Madeira

name: Relógios
summary: An account of the public clocks of Madeira, above all the clock of Funchal Cathedral: the old clock made in 1775 and its replacement given by Dr Michael Grabham, installed in 1921–22. It also lists the other public clocks on the islands and records the earlier custom of a paid official striking the hours.

name: Sanatórios da Madeira
summary: Tuberculosis sanatoria at Monte, Funchal, arising from the Hohenlohe concession of 1903. The Elucidário records the diplomatic dispute that led the Portuguese State to buy back the concession in 1909. It also reproduces Dr António de Lencastre's 1903 report and a 1914 government notice leasing the confiscated properties at Monte.
location: parish of Monte, municipality of Funchal

name: Câmara de Lôbos
summary: Parish west of Funchal. The Elucidário traces its name to Zarco's discovery voyage and describes its churches, chapels and collegiate chapter, early settlers, fishing community and renowned vineyards. It also records the parish's localities, boundaries, levadas and population.
location: parish of Câmara de Lobos, municipality of Câmara de Lobos

name: Grande
summary: Peak of about 1,600 m among the heights surrounding the parish of Serra de Água.
location: heights surrounding the parish of Serra de Água

name: Grande
summary: Mountain in Madeira's central range, not far from Pico Ruivo.
location: central mountain range of Madeira, near Pico Ruivo

name: Grande
summary: Stream that is a tributary of the Ribeira de Machico.
location: municipality of Machico (tributary of the Ribeira de Machico)

name: Ribeiras
summary: General term for Madeira's streams, which rise on the central mountain range and run through deep, narrow valleys to the sea. They are torrential in winter and often dry in summer. The Elucidário describes their destructive floods and lists the island's principal streams.

name: Fajãs
summary: General term for fajãs, flats of land formed by landslides in Madeira. The Elucidário lists the best-known examples and records notable landslips of 1689, 1804, 1856 and 1894.

name: Frigorifico
summary: Cold store in Funchal planned by the Junta Agrícola. It was built at considerable cost but never put into operation, and was abandoned in 1918.
location: municipality of Funchal

name: Costas
summary: The two coasts of Madeira: the north coast (Costa do Norte) and the south coast (Costa do Sul). They are divided by the mountain range running east to west across the island, with a rugged interior between them.

name: Mercado e Capela de São Sebastião
aliases: Mercado e Capela de São Sebastião
summary: Ancient chapel of São Sebastião in Funchal, demolished in 1803 by Governor D. José Manuel da Câmara to build a market. The people rebuilt it in 1821, but it had been demolished again by 1827. Its square, now Largo do Comércio, has a marble fountain.
location: Largo do Comércio, Funchal

name: Nossa Senhora das Dores
summary: Dedication shared by several Madeiran chapels to Our Lady of Sorrows. They include the cemetery chapels of Santa Cruz, Câmara de Lobos and Angústias (Funchal). Another is the chapel of the Hospício da Princesa Dona Maria Amélia, whose image was given by Maximilian, later Emperor of Mexico.

name: Cais do Ilhéu de Fora
summary: Small quay on the Ilhéu de Fora, built in 1870 for the lighthouse staff. The same entry also notes the Abra quay (1905) and the Caniçal landing stage (1909).
location: Ilhéu de Fora, parish of Caniçal, municipality of Machico

name: Cais da Ponta da Oliveira
summary: Landing stage at Ponta da Oliveira, built in 1909. The same entry also notes the Lazareto quay, probably built between 1866 and 1874.
location: Ponta da Oliveira, municipality of Funchal

name: Cais do Salto do Cavalo
summary: Private quay at Salto do Cavalo, built by the industrialist Pedro da Cunha Pires.
location: Salto do Cavalo

name: Cais do “Palace Hotel”
summary: Quay of the Palace Hotel on the Estrada Monumental. The same entry also notes the Wilson Company quay near Quinta do Calaça, built around 1903.
location: Estrada Monumental, municipality of Funchal

name: Cais da Ponta da Cruz
summary: Quay at Ponta da Cruz with an older part and a modern part. The modern part was built around 1910 by the local cannery owners.
location: Ponta da Cruz, municipality of Funchal

name: Cais de Câmara de Lobos
summary: Quay at Câmara de Lobos, begun by the government in 1876 and enlarged by the Junta Geral in 1903.
location: parish and municipality of Câmara de Lobos

name: Cais da Campanário
summary: Small landing stage at Campanário, built by the Junta Geral in 1908.
location: parish of Campanário, municipality of Ribeira Brava

name: Cais do Pesqueiro
summary: Landing stage at Pesqueiro, built by the Junta Geral in 1916.

name: Cais do Porto do Moniz
summary: Quay at Porto Moniz, built by the Junta Geral in 1916. It replaced a natural landing and a passenger ladder.
location: parish and municipality of Porto Moniz

name: Cais do Seixal
summary: Quay at Seixal, built by the Junta Geral between 1903 and 1916.
location: parish of Seixal, municipality of Porto Moniz

name: Cais de S. Jorge
summary: Quay at São Jorge, built by the Junta Geral between 1904 and 1910. The same entry also notes the Pedra da Pescaria quay at Faial, built by the Junta Geral between 1903 and 1905.
location: municipality of Santana

name: Cais do Porto da Cruz
summary: Quay at Porto da Cruz, built in 1903. The same entry also notes the Ilhéu de Cima quay in Porto Santo, built around 1902 for the lighthouse staff.
location: parish of Porto da Cruz, municipality of Machico

name: Porto do Moniz
summary: Parish on Madeira's north-west coast and one of the oldest northern parishes, founded around the estate and chapel of Francisco Moniz, the Elder. The Elucidário covers the origin of its name, its churches and chapels, and the fort built against corsairs. It also records its localities and population.
location: parish and municipality of Porto Moniz, north-west coast of Madeira

name: Pico dos Barcelos.
summary: Inhabited locality and small hill in Santo António parish, famous as a viewpoint over the bay from Garajau to Cabo Girão. Its name probably comes from the early settler Diogo Barcelos.
location: sítio in the parish of Santo António, municipality of Funchal

name: Cumiada Alta
summary: Cumiada Alta is a high ridge on Madeira, rising above 1,700 metres near Pico Ruivo and the basalt column known as Homem em Pé. The Elucidário notes it for its rare plants.
location: near Pico Ruivo, Madeira

name: Cumiada de S. Vicente
summary: The Cumiada de S. Vicente is a ridge at about 1,000 metres from which both the north and south coasts of Madeira can be seen. It was reached by a road opened in 1916, and a very rare clubmoss grows there.
location: municipality of Câmara de Lobos, Madeira

name: Praça de São João
summary: The Praça de São João was a very old square in Funchal beside the Campo da Barca. It was demolished before 1860, and its site now forms part of the Praça de Tenerife.
location: beside the Campo da Barca, Funchal

name: Cortado
summary: Cortado is a locality between Santana and Faial. It is noted for its fine views over Faial and the Penha de Águia, and for its green, wooded road.
location: between Santana and Faial, municipality of Santana

name: São Pedro
summary: São Pedro is the most populous of Funchal's four urban parishes and the place where Zargo made the first settlement. The parish was created in 1566, suppressed in 1579 and restored in 1587. The Elucidário covers its clergy stipends, church building, chapels, notable institutions and boundaries.
location: urban parish of São Pedro, municipality of Funchal

name: ilha da Madeira
summary: Madeira is the main island of the archipelago of the same name. The Elucidário's general survey covers its position, relief, streams, towns, scenery, roads, products, fauna, minerals, irrigation, trade and industries, and the origins, physical types and customs of its people. It serves as the umbrella article for the more detailed 'Madeira' sub-entries.

name: Posto de Desinfecção do Campo da Barca
aliases: Posto de Desinfecção do Campo da Barca
summary: The Posto de Desinfecção do Campo da Barca was Funchal's public disinfection station, built in 1904 and opened in 1905 by the Junta Geral. It disinfected homes and public buildings after cases of contagious disease, notably during epidemics.
location: Campo da Barca, Funchal

name: Capela de Nossa Senhora da Paz
summary: The Capela de Nossa Senhora da Paz is a chapel in Funchal founded in 1621 by the priest Jerónimo da Silva.
location: parish of Santa Maria Maior, municipality of Funchal

name: Enseada, Porto e Cais de Machico
summary: The bay of Machico is one of the widest and most picturesque bays of the Madeira archipelago. The Elucidário describes its harbour and landing quays, recording successive quays built in 1870–1873, 1905 and 1907 and harbour lights installed in 1931.
location: parish and municipality of Machico, Madeira

name: Porto ou Portinho da Morena
summary: The Porto or Portinho da Morena is a small landing place on the south-south-west coast of Porto Santo.
location: south-south-west coast of Porto Santo

name: Planaltos
summary: This entry concerns Madeira's few upland plateaux. It quotes a Portuguese dictionary that names four of them: Santo da Serra, Achada de Santa Ana, Paul da Serra and Achadas da Cruz.

name: Montepio
summary: The Montepio was a former charitable house in Funchal for poor and respectable widows. It was founded by João de Carvalhal in 1825 or 1826.
location: Funchal

name: Monumentos
summary: This is the Elucidário's introductory heading to brief notes on the few public monuments of Madeira.

name: Monumento à Constituição de 1821
summary: The Monumento à Constituição de 1821 was an unfinished monument in Funchal to the 1821 Constitution. It was demolished in 1823, and its foundations held a time capsule.
location: Funchal

name: Monumento a Câmara Pestana
summary: This monument is a bronze bust of the bacteriologist Luís da Câmara Pestana, erected in 1906 in the asylum garden in São Gonçalo. A plaque was also placed on his birthplace in 1913.
location: asylum garden, parish of São Gonçalo, municipality of Funchal

name: Monumento comemorativo do Bombardeamento do Funchal
aliases: Monumento comemorativo do Bombardeamento do Funchal
summary: This is a small memorial to the bombardment of Funchal, standing in the old Angústias cemetery.
location: old Angústias cemetery, Funchal

name: Monumento aos Aviadore
summary: This monument in Funchal's Jardim Municipal commemorates the 1921 Lisbon–Funchal flight of Gago Coutinho and Sacadura Cabral.
location: Jardim Municipal, Funchal

name: Monumento a João Fernandes Vieira
summary: This is a modest bust of João Fernandes Vieira, inaugurated in 1924 on Avenida Arriaga in Funchal. Nine years later it was moved to the Jardim Municipal.
location: Jardim Municipal, Funchal

name: São Vicente
summary: São Vicente is described as the largest and most populous parish of northern Madeira and the seat of the only town on the north coast. The Elucidário covers its settlement, church history, localities and landscape, and the deadly landslide of 1929.
location: parish and municipality of São Vicente, north coast of Madeira

name: Capela de Nossa Senhora do Perpétuo Socorro
aliases: Nossa Senhora do Perpétuo Socorro (Capela de)
summary: This chapel dedicated to Nossa Senhora do Perpétuo Socorro was built at the sítio da Queimada by Francisco de Freitas Correia. The year 1244 printed for it predates the settlement of Madeira and is presumably a misprint.
location: sítio da Queimada, parish of Água de Pena

name: Cabos
summary: This entry describes Madeira's two capes, Cabo Garajau and Cabo Girão, covering their names, geology and botanical interest.

name: Desertas
summary: The Desertas are a group of three small uninhabited islands, Ilhéu Chão, Deserta Grande and Bugio, lying south-east of Madeira near the Ponta de São Lourenço. The Elucidário gives their position, distances, ecclesiastical attachment, history of ownership and sources.
location: south-east of Madeira, near the Ponta de São Lourenço

name: Arquipélago da Madeira
summary: This entry surveys the Madeira archipelago as a whole: its historical importance, composition, geographical position, extreme points, area, coastline, dimensions and population. It points to separate entries on the individual islands and the Funchal district.

name: Ribeira e Porto de São Bartolomeu
summary: The Ribeira de São Bartolomeu is a stream that rises on the Paul da Serra and divides the parishes of Calheta and Estreito da Calheta. There is a small landing place at its mouth.
location: boundary between the parishes of Calheta and Estreito da Calheta, municipality of Calheta

name: Forte de S. Felipe da Praça
aliases: Forte de S. Felipe da Praça
summary: The Forte de S. Felipe da Praça was a fort in Funchal built in 1628 by the bishop-governor D. Jerónimo Fernando. It was later sold and replaced by a warehouse.
location: between the mouths of the João Gomes and Santa Luzia streams, Funchal

name: Forte de Santo António da Alfândega
aliases: Forte de Santo António da Alfândega
summary: A fort in Funchal, Madeira. It was a redoubt built in 1644–45 on the walls of the Customs House to cover the beach with crossfire. It was later converted into warehouses.
location: On the walls of the Customs House, Funchal

name: Forte de S. Pedro
summary: The Forte de S. Pedro, also called Forte Novo, stood on the Calhau wall in Funchal. It was finished in 1707 under Duarte Sodré Pereira and was notable for its furnace for heating shot. It was demolished in 1897.
location: On the Calhau wall, Funchal

name: Forte da Penha de França
summary: An outwork built in 1712 to defend the Ribeiro Seco cove in Funchal. British troops were quartered there in 1801.
location: Ribeiro Seco cove, Funchal

name: Forte de Loures
summary: A 17th-century fort in Funchal covering the Gonçalo Aires cove, traditionally said to have been built by a private individual. Captain-General D. Diogo Coutinho wished to establish a silk factory there.
location: Gonçalo Aires cove, Funchal

name: Forte de S. João Baptista
summary: A fort built in 1708 on a rocky point east of Machico bay. It fired on a Miguelist brig in 1828 and became a cholera hospital in 1910.
location: Rocky point east of Machico bay, parish and municipality of Machico

name: Forte de Nª Sª do Amparo
aliases: Forte de Nª Sª do Amparo
summary: A triangular fort at Machico built in 1706 at no cost to the Crown. It was the last fort to surrender to the Miguelist landing of 1828.
location: Parish and municipality of Machico

name: Forte de S. Roque de Machico
aliases: Forte de S. Roque de Machico
summary: A fort built during the Philippine period at the mouth of the Ribeirinho in Machico bay. Only fragments of its walls remain.
location: Mouth of the Ribeirinho, Machico bay, parish and municipality of Machico

name: Forte do Caniçal
summary: A fort overlooking the Caniçal cove, in the municipality of Machico. It was built in the early 18th century after a pirate landing there.
location: Caniçal cove, parish of Caniçal, municipality of Machico

name: Forte de S. Bento da Ribeira Brava
aliases: Forte de S. Bento da Ribeira Brava
summary: A fort built by Governor Duarte Sodré Pereira to defend Ribeira Brava.
location: Parish and municipality of Ribeira Brava

name: Quedas de Água
summary: The Elucidário entry lists the best-known waterfalls on Madeira island. They are grouped by the streams and valleys where they occur.

name: Queimada
summary: An inhabited locality in Água de Pena, municipality of Machico. It has Madeira's first chapel dedicated to Our Lady of Perpetual Help, dating from 1924.
location: Sítio in Água de Pena, municipality of Machico

name: Rua da Queimada de Cima
summary: A street in Funchal, formerly called Rua do Oliveira and Rua Afonso Vaz. In 1921 it was notorious for its insanitary stables for hire horses and draught animals.
location: Funchal

name: Queimado
summary: A peak in Madeira on the boundary between Ribeira Brava and São Vicente. It lies between Lombo do Mouro and Monte Medonho.
location: On the boundary of Ribeira Brava and São Vicente, between Lombo do Mouro and Monte Medonho

name: Rua de Júlio da Silva Carvalho
summary: A street in Madeira named after Júlio da Silva Carvalho, with its own entry in the Elucidário.

name: Paços do Concelho
summary: The town hall of Funchal, an eighteenth-century palace on Rua do Comércio bought by the municipal council in 1883. The Elucidário also traces the many buildings the council occupied from the fifteenth century onwards. It adds brief notes on the town halls of the other Madeiran municipalities.
location: Rua do Comércio, parish of Santa Luzia, municipality of Funchal

name: Quinta do Palheiro do Ferreiro
summary: An estate in the municipality of Funchal, described by the Elucidário as the finest and largest in Madeira. It was created by the 1st Count of Carvalhal in the early nineteenth century and later owned by John Blandy. The entry records royal visits and quotes an English visitor's description of 1826.
location: Municipality of Funchal

name: Capelas das Almas
summary: Chapels in Madeira dedicated to the Souls in Purgatory, located in Ribeira Brava, Estreito de Câmara de Lobos, Calheta and Ponta do Sol. Several of them have been lost or demolished.
location: Parish of Estreito de Câmara de Lobos, municipality of Câmara de Lobos, among other places

name: Branco
summary: Pico Branco is a mountain in the north-east of Porto Santo island. It rises to 420 m above sea level.
location: North-east of Porto Santo island

name: Igrejas Inglesas
summary: The Protestant churches of Funchal. They comprise the Anglican church in Rua da Bela Vista (completed 1822), a second Anglican church in Rua dos Aranhas (1848) and the Scottish church.
location: Funchal

name: Rua da Igrejinha
summary: A former street in Funchal running between Largo do Colégio and Rua das Pretas. It was named after the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Piedade, known as the 'Igrejinha', which was founded in 1613 and demolished in 1836.
location: Between Largo do Colégio and Rua das Pretas, Funchal

name: Moinhos
summary: An inhabited locality in the parish of Caniço. It contains the ruins of a chapel of Nossa Senhora da Salvação founded in 1614.
location: Sítio in the parish of Caniço, municipality of Santa Cruz

name: Ribeira dos Moinhos
summary: A stream that crosses the parish of Boaventura. It reaches the sea near the Ribeira do Porco.
location: Parish of Boaventura, municipality of São Vicente

name: Ribeira dos Moinhos
summary: A stream in the parish of Ponta do Pargo, Madeira.
location: Parish of Ponta do Pargo, municipality of Calheta

name: Rua dos Moinhos
summary: A former name of part of Rua das Mercês in Funchal. It was named after a mill that once stood there, and the street was originally called Rua do Peso.
location: Part of Rua das Mercês, Funchal

name: Mole
