summary: A small islet off the coast of the parish of Porto Moniz, Madeira.
location: Off the coast of the parish of Porto Moniz, municipality of Porto Moniz

name: Mirantes
summary: The Elucidário's entry on the viewpoints (mirantes or miradouros) of Madeira. It lists those in Funchal and elsewhere and recalls the viewpoints recommended by Civil Governor José Silvestre Ribeiro in 1850.
location: Madeira

name: Manuel de Castro
aliases: Manuel de Castro (Rampa e ponte de D.)
summary: A ramp and bridge in Funchal named after D. Manuel de Portugal e Castro, governor from 1823 to 1825. He built the bridge and widened the ramp.
location: Funchal, Madeira

name: Vapor
summary: The 'Vapor' was a curious red wooden building spanning the Santa Luzia stream in Funchal. It was built in 1837 as a café and bathhouse and was demolished around 1898.
location: Over the Santa Luzia stream, Funchal, Madeira

name: Monumentos Nacionais
summary: The Elucidário's list of buildings and works of art in the Funchal district classified as national monuments or as properties of public interest. The classifications were made under decrees published in the Diário do Governo in 1940 and 1943.
location: District of Funchal

name: Ilha da Deserta Grande ou somente Deserta
aliases: Deserta Grande ou somente Deserta (Ilha da)
summary: The largest of the three Desertas islands: steep, nearly flat-topped and with scant brackish water. It was never permanently inhabited but was used for hunting, orchil gathering, grazing and some cereal growing. The entry covers its geography, history and fauna, including a corsair attack in 1503 and a landslide in 1894.
location: Desertas islands, Madeira archipelago

name: Costa de Baixo
summary: The popular name for Madeira's south coast west of Funchal. It covers the municipalities of Câmara de Lobos, Ribeira Brava, Ponta do Sol and Calheta.
location: South coast of Madeira west of Funchal

name: Costa de Cima
summary: The popular name for Madeira's south coast east of Funchal. It covers the municipalities of Santa Cruz and Machico, except the north-coast parish of Porto da Cruz.
location: South coast of Madeira east of Funchal (municipalities of Santa Cruz and Machico)

name: Mercados
summary: The Elucidário's entry on Funchal's public markets, chiefly the Mercado de S. João. That market opened in 1823 on land leased from the Franciscans and was demolished in 1883 to make way for the municipal theatre.
location: Funchal, Madeira

name: Pedro V
summary: The Mercado de D. Pedro V, a public market in Funchal. It was built from 1876 with municipal loans and opened on 19 December 1880.
location: Funchal, Madeira

name: Portos da Madeira
summary: A survey of the ports and landing places of the Madeira archipelago, graded as good, tolerable or poor. It notes recent improvements and includes a 1944 report on planned harbour works.
location: Madeira archipelago

name: Académica
summary: Former name of a large open space in Funchal, now the Campo do Almirante Reis. It was built in 1837 with the proceeds of a student theatrical performance celebrating Queen Maria II's marriage. It was later landscaped and given a children's park, opened in 1939.
location: Funchal, Madeira

name: Capelas de Santana
summary: The Elucidário's list of chapels in Madeira dedicated to Saint Anne (Santana). It gives their parishes, founders and foundation dates where known, ranging from 1607 to 1790.
location: Madeira

name: Ribeira da Boaventura
summary: The Boaventura stream, also called Ribeira de São Pedro. It rises west of Pico das Abóboras in the municipality of Santa Cruz.
location: Municipality of Santa Cruz, Madeira

name: Ribeira da Caniço
summary: The Caniço stream on Madeira. It rises at Camacha and receives the Vale Paraíso brook.
location: Madeira; rises at Camacha

name: Ribeira de Gonçalo Aires
summary: The Gonçalo Aires stream on Madeira. It rises at Pico do Infante and carries little water.
location: Madeira; rises at Pico do Infante

name: Ribeira de Santa Luzia
summary: The Santa Luzia stream on Madeira, also called Ribeira da Praça. It rises at Pico do Areeiro and Pico Escalvado.
location: Madeira; rises at Pico do Areeiro and Pico Escalvado

name: João
summary: The São João stream in Funchal. It rises at Pico Escalvado and Pico de Santo António and has borne many former names.
location: Funchal, Madeira

name: Ribeira dos Socorridos
summary: The Socorridos stream on Madeira. It rises at the Torrinhas, and its tributaries include the Ribeira de Vasco Gil.
location: Madeira; rises at the Torrinhas

name: Ribeira do Vigario
summary: The Vigário stream, also called Ribeira de Câmara de Lobos. It rises at Achada do Poiso.
location: Municipality of Câmara de Lobos, Madeira

name: Ribeira do Campanário
summary: The Campanário stream on Madeira, also called Ribeira da Lapa. It rises at Pico dos Ferreiros and carries little water.
location: Madeira; rises at Pico dos Ferreiros

name: Ribeira Brava
summary: The Ribeira Brava stream on Madeira. It rises at the São Vicente ridge, and the Elucidário lists its tributaries.
location: Madeira; rises at the São Vicente ridge

name: Ribeira da Tabua
summary: The Tabua stream on Madeira. It rises at Pico das Pedras and receives the Barqueiro brook.
location: Madeira; rises at Pico das Pedras

name: Ribeira da Serra de Água da Calheta
aliases: Ribeira da Serra de Água da Calheta
summary: The Serra de Água stream of Calheta on Madeira. It shares its source with the Madalena stream and receives three brooks.
location: Calheta, Madeira

name: Ribeira da Calheta
summary: The Calheta stream on Madeira. It rises at the Cabeço da Levadinha (Lombo do Salão) and receives the Cutileiro and Convento brooks.
location: Calheta, Madeira

name: Bartolomeu
summary: The São Bartolomeu stream on Madeira. It rises at Pico Gordo and Pico da Silva, and its main tributary is the Farrobo brook.
location: Madeira; rises at Pico Gordo and Pico da Silva

name: Baixa do Atanasio
summary: Baixa do Atanásio is a shoal near the bay of Câmara de Lobos, on the south coast of Madeira.
location: shoal near the bay of Câmara de Lobos, parish and municipality of Câmara de Lobos, Madeira

name: Camara de Lôbos
summary: Câmara de Lobos is a municipality of Madeira whose seat was historically a 'lugar' rather than a vila. The Elucidário quotes Gaspar Frutuoso's description of it and outlines the creation of the concelho in 1835 and later changes to its parishes.
location: municipality of Câmara de Lobos, Madeira

name: Gorda
summary: Ponta Gorda is a small coastal point in São Martinho parish, Funchal, near the Gorgulho islet and Ponta da Cruz.
location: coastal point in the parish of São Martinho, municipality of Funchal, near the Gorgulho islet and Ponta da Cruz

name: Gordo
summary: Pico Gordo is a peak of 1,200 metres in the uplands of Calheta parish, near Monte das Estrebarias.
location: uplands of the parish of Calheta, municipality of Calheta, near Monte das Estrebarias

name: Conventos
summary: The Elucidário's entry on convents lists the Franciscan houses of Madeira: four friaries and three nunneries, most of them now gone. It also mentions the Jesuit college in Funchal, now used as a barracks.

name: Campanario
summary: Campanário is a parish on Madeira's south coast, west of Cabo Girão, named after an islet shaped like a bell tower. The Elucidário covers its church history, early settlers, Jesuit estates and notable natives, and records its transfer from Câmara de Lobos to the new municipality of Ribeira Brava in 1914.
location: parish on the south coast west of Cabo Girão, municipality of Ribeira Brava, Madeira

name: Ilhéu, Porto e Ribeira de Porto da Cruz
aliases: Porto da Cruz (Ilhéu, Porto e Ribeira de)
summary: These are three coastal features of Porto da Cruz parish that share its name: an islet, a small harbour whose landing place is called Furna, and a stream that flows into the sea nearby.
location: coast of the parish of Porto da Cruz, Madeira

name: Pico da Cruz
summary: This Pico da Cruz is a 936 m peak between the parishes of Câmara de Lobos and Estreito, noted for its wide panoramic view.
location: between the parishes of Câmara de Lobos and Estreito, municipality of Câmara de Lobos

name: Pico da Cruz
summary: This Pico da Cruz is a small hill about 100 m high in the parish of Campanário.
location: parish of Campanário, Madeira

name: Pico da Cruz
summary: This Pico da Cruz is a 263 m coastal hill in São Martinho, formerly called Pico do Telégrafo, with fine views over Funchal and its bay.
location: parish of São Martinho, municipality of Funchal

name: Pico da Cruz
summary: This Pico da Cruz is one of the highest heights surrounding the parish of Serra de Água.
location: heights around the parish of Serra de Água, municipality of Ribeira Brava

name: Ponta da Cruz
summary: This Ponta da Cruz is a headland in São Martinho regarded as the western limit of Funchal bay. It was once the site of a small redoubt and lies near a fish-canning factory.
location: headland in the parish of São Martinho, municipality of Funchal, western limit of Funchal bay

name: Ponta da Cruz
summary: This Ponta da Cruz is a small point on the northern coast of Porto Santo.
location: northern coast of Porto Santo

name: Ribeira da Cruz
summary: Ribeira da Cruz is a stream that rises at Pico da Pedreira and flows between Ponta do Pargo and Achadas da Cruz to the sea near Fajã da Rocha.
location: between Ponta do Pargo and Achadas da Cruz, municipality of Calheta

name: Cantim
summary: Cape Cantim is a point on the Moroccan coast at the latitude of Madeira. It is the African point closest to the archipelago, about 350 miles away.
location: Moroccan coast, about 350 miles from Madeira

name: Vales
summary: This short entry on the valleys of Madeira quotes a lyrical passage from the Diccionario Universal Ilustrado Portuguez. The passage singles out the valleys of Machico, Funchal (with Vale Formoso), Jardim da Serra, São Vicente and Penha de Águia.

name: Pico do Facho
summary: This Pico do Facho is a 330 m peak overlooking Machico. It was once the site of a semaphore station and has a spring said to rise and fall with the tide.
location: peak overlooking Machico, municipality of Machico

name: Pico do Facho.
summary: This Pico do Facho is the highest mountain on Porto Santo, at 500 m, in the north of the island.
location: north of the island of Porto Santo

name: Capela do Sagrado Coração de Jesus
summary: The Elucidário records two chapels dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus: one at Cardais in Água de Pena, dating from 1907, and one in Monte.
location: Cardais, parish of Água de Pena; and Monte

name: Santa Cruz
summary: Santa Cruz is a parish and one of Madeira's oldest settlements, named after a cross Zarco had raised there at the discovery. The Elucidário covers its early ecclesiastical history, collegiate church, chapels, noble settlers and localities.
location: parish of Santa Cruz, municipality of Santa Cruz, Madeira

name: Ponta, Porto e Cais da Ponta do Sol
aliases: Ponta do Sol (Ponta, Porto e Cais da)
summary: This entry describes the headland, small harbour and quay of Ponta do Sol on Madeira's south-west coast, and the possible origin of the name. The quay was built by the municipal council in 1848–1850; an extension project of 1880 was never carried out.
location: south-west coast, parish and municipality of Ponta do Sol, Madeira

name: Porto Santo
summary: This entry describes the relief of Porto Santo island. It covers its hilly terrain, its main peaks with their heights, its two small plains and the chief headlands of its coast.
location: island of Porto Santo

name: Portas da Cidade
summary: The Portas da Cidade were the gates in Funchal's old city walls. The Elucidário lists those still standing in 1836 and when each was demolished, and gives older references from 1597, King Sebastião's fortification regulations and Frutuoso.
location: old city walls of Funchal

name: Forte do Porto da Cruz
summary: The fort of Porto da Cruz was built in 1708 and dismantled in 1804. The same entry notes the Fort of Santo António at Paul do Mar, built in 1754.
location: Porto da Cruz, Madeira

name: Forte de S. Jorge da Calheta
aliases: Forte de S. Jorge da Calheta
summary: The Fort of São Jorge was a fort at Calheta. The Elucidário briefly records its captain in 1751.
location: Calheta, municipality of Calheta, Madeira

name: Reduto de S. Jorge
summary: The Reduto de S. Jorge was a redoubt in the parish of São Jorge, Madeira. The Elucidário gives only a brief note on it, recording who its captain was in 1785.
location: parish of São Jorge, Madeira

name: Forte de S. Francisco
summary: The Forte de S. Francisco is a fort in Santa Cruz, Madeira. It was built in 1749 by order of the bishop-governor D. Fr. João do Nascimento and paid for with militia fines.
location: Santa Cruz, municipality of Santa Cruz, Madeira

name: Forte de S. José da Ilha do Porto Santo
aliases: Forte de S. José da Ilha do Porto Santo
summary: The Forte de S. José is a fort in the town of Porto Santo. It was built under Pombal's government and included a residence for the governors. In 1921 it was ceded to the fiscal guard.
location: town of Porto Santo, island of Porto Santo

name: Porto de Laje
summary: The Porto de Laje is a small landing place on the coast of Seixal parish, Madeira.
location: coast of the parish of Seixal, Madeira

name: Capelas de Nossa Senhora do Rosário
summary: This entry covers the chapels dedicated to Our Lady of the Rosary in several Madeiran parishes, including São Roque in Funchal. The Elucidário lists their founders and dates of foundation.
location: various parishes of Madeira, including São Roque, municipality of Funchal

name: Capelas de Nossa Senhora da Salvação
summary: This entry covers two chapels of Our Lady of Salvation. One, at Moinhos in Caniço, was founded in 1614 and is now in ruins; the other is in Funchal.
location: Moinhos, parish of Caniço, municipality of Santa Cruz (one chapel); Funchal (the other)

name: Capela de Nossa Senhora da Saúde do Monte Olivete
aliases: Nossa Senhora da Saúde do Monte Olivete (Capela de)
summary: The Capela de Nossa Senhora da Saúde do Monte Olivete was a chapel in the parish of Santa Maria Maior, Funchal, which no longer exists. It was built on an entail founded by Pedro Lopes de Vasconcelos in 1675.
location: parish of Santa Maria Maior, municipality of Funchal

name: Capela de Nossa Senhora do Terço
summary: The Capela de Nossa Senhora do Terço is a chapel beside the parish church of Machico. It was built by the people of Machico in 1770.
location: beside the parish church, Machico, municipality of Machico

name: Capela de Nossa Senhora do Vale
summary: The Capela de Nossa Senhora do Vale is a chapel at Vale Formoso, in the parish of Santa Luzia, Funchal. It was founded and endowed by António Vogado in 1726.
location: Vale Formoso, parish of Santa Luzia, municipality of Funchal

name: Ribeira da Calheta
summary: The Ribeira da Calheta, also called Ribeira da Vila da Calheta, is a stream that flows into the town of Calheta. It is fed by several small tributaries.
location: town of Calheta, municipality of Calheta

name: Real
summary: Praça Real was the name given under D. Miguel to Funchal's Praça da Constituição, now part of Avenida Dr. Manuel de Arriaga. Troops paraded there on feast days.
location: Avenida Dr. Manuel de Arriaga, Funchal

name: Monumento a Nossa Senhora da Paz
aliases: Monumento a Nossa Senhora da Paz
summary: The Monumento a Nossa Senhora da Paz is a marble statue of Our Lady of Peace with bronze reliefs and an adjoining chapel, at the Terreiro da Luta in Monte. It was begun in 1923 and inaugurated in 1927 through the efforts of Father José Marques Jardim.
location: Terreiro da Luta, parish of Monte, municipality of Funchal

name: Monumento ao Sagrado Coração de Jesus
aliases: Monumento ao Sagrado Coração de Jesus
summary: The Monumento ao Sagrado Coração de Jesus is a statue of the Sacred Heart of Jesus at Ponta do Garajau, Caniço. It was erected by Aires de Ornelas de Vasconcelos and blessed in 1927.
location: Ponta do Garajau, parish of Caniço, municipality of Santa Cruz

name: Monumento a João Gonçalves Zargo
summary: The Monumento a João Gonçalves Zargo is a bronze statue of Zargo, first captain-donatary of Funchal, by Francisco Franco. It was inaugurated on the Avenida Arriaga, Funchal, in 1934.
location: Avenida Arriaga, Funchal

name: Monumento aos mortos da Grande Guerra
aliases: Monumento aos mortos da Grande Guerra
summary: The Monumento aos mortos da Grande Guerra is a small memorial in Funchal to those killed in the First World War. Its foundation stone was laid in 1935.
location: Funchal

name: Monumento ao Doutor Teles
summary: The Monumento ao Doutor Teles is a modest monument in the gardens of the Asilo de Mendicidade e Órfãos, Funchal. It honours Dr Alexandre da Cunha Teles, a benefactor of charitable services, and was inaugurated in 1939.
location: gardens of the Asilo de Mendicidade e Órfãos, Funchal

name: Outeiro
summary: Outeiro is an inhabited locality in the parish of Canhas, Madeira. It had a former chapel dating from 1733 and has a recent chapel of the Sacred Heart.
location: sítio in the parish of Canhas, Madeira

name: Calheta
summary: Calheta is a town and municipality in western Madeira, created by royal charter of 1 July 1502. It later became the seat of a countship granted to the captains of Funchal and was reorganised as a concelho in 1835.
location: western Madeira

name: Águas
summary: This entry is a survey of the use of irrigation water in Madeira from settlement onwards. It covers the building of levadas, the royal charters regulating water rights from the fifteenth century, and the State's later role in constructing levadas.

name: Guiomar
summary: The Mirante de D. Guiomar is a belvedere at the Quinta das Angústias in Funchal, used as a landmark for anchoring. It is named after D. Guiomar Madalena Acciaioly, whose goods were seized for debts to the Treasury around 1800.
location: Quinta das Angústias, Funchal

name: Palácio de S. Lourenço
summary: The Palácio de S. Lourenço in Funchal was originally the fortress of São Lourenço. It served as the residence of the governors and military commanders of Madeira, and the Elucidário records its successive alterations, its chapel and its state rooms.
location: Funchal

name: Quinta do Salvador
summary: Quinta do Salvador is an inhabited locality in the parish of Monte, Funchal. It contains the Quinta da Paz, with its chapel of Nossa Senhora do Livramento.
location: sítio in the parish of Monte, municipality of Funchal

name: Casas de Romeiros
summary: The Casas de Romeiros were pilgrims' shelters built at Monte, at Santo António da Serra and at Piedade on the Ponta de São Lourenço. The Elucidário gives notes on their history.
location: Monte, Santo António da Serra and Piedade on the Ponta de São Lourenço, Madeira

name: Ilhéus do Faial
summary: The Ilhéus do Faial are a group of small islets and rocks off the coast of Faial parish, Madeira, known collectively by that name.
location: off the coast of the parish of Faial, Madeira

name: Ribeira do Faial
summary: The Ribeira do Faial is a stream that rises near Pico Ruivo and reaches the sea at Faial. It is crossed by the longest bridge in Madeira, built between 1907 and 1910.
location: from near Pico Ruivo to the sea at Faial, Madeira

name: Faial
summary: Faial is a locality in the parish of Santa Maria Maior, Funchal. The Elucidário records its chapel of Nossa Senhora da Natividade, founded by Zenobio Acciaioli in 1582.
location: sítio in the parish of Santa Maria Maior, municipality of Funchal

name: Fajã
summary: Fajã is a Madeiran term for fertile tracts of land formed by landslides, found both inland and along the coast. The Elucidário notes that it is a common element in place-names.
location: Madeira

name: Fajã
summary: Fajã is an inhabited locality in the parish of Arco da Calheta. The Elucidário records the ruins of a chapel of Nossa Senhora da Boa Hora there.
location: sítio in the parish of Arco da Calheta, municipality of Calheta

name: Fajã
summary: Fajã is an inhabited locality in the parish of Santo António, Funchal, on the left bank of the Ribeira dos Socorridos.
location: sítio in the parish of Santo António, municipality of Funchal, on the left bank of the Ribeira dos Socorridos

name: Cinco de Junho
summary: Rua Cinco de Junho is a Funchal street linking Rua dos Aranhas (now Rua Dr. Chaves) with Largo do Ribeiro Real. It was opened when the old cemetery alleys were demolished, and is named after 5 June 1834, the date on which the constitutional government was proclaimed in Madeira.
location: street in Funchal, between Rua dos Aranhas (now Dr. Chaves) and Largo do Ribeiro Real

name: Nomes de Ruas
summary: Nomes de Ruas is an essay on the naming of streets in Funchal. It recalls the municipal council's resolution of 19 June 1890 to name new streets after illustrious Madeirans and laments that this was seldom followed. It lists notable Madeirans still uncommemorated in 1921 and urges restraint in renaming old streets.
location: Funchal

name: Caminho de Luis Miranda
summary: Caminho de Luís Miranda was the name, from 1896 to 1910, of the road between the parish church of Santo António and the Ribeira. It honoured Luís de Bettencourt Miranda, long-serving secretary of the Funchal council.
location: road in the parish of Santo António, municipality of Funchal, between the parish church and the Ribeira

name: Madeira
summary: This sub-entry of the Elucidário's survey of Madeira deals with coastal hydrography. It refers readers to the article on islets and lists the named reefs or shoals (baixas) around the Madeiran coast.
location: coast of Madeira

name: Ilha do Porto Santo
summary: Porto Santo is an island of the Madeira archipelago. The Elucidário describes its name, size, position, relief, beach, springs, administration and governors, settlement, vegetation, crops, geology and population. It stresses the island's poverty in water and its potential as a spa and bathing resort.
location: island of Porto Santo, municipality of Porto Santo

name: Praça do Peixe
summary: The Praça do Peixe, or Praça de São Pedro, was Funchal's fish market. It began as a small market built by the Câmara in 1817 and was replaced by a building opened in 1840, which was later demolished for the Avenida do Mar.
location: Funchal

name: Alfândega de Machico
summary: The customs house of Machico was created by royal charter in 1477, together with those of Funchal and Santa Cruz. Although it stood at the seat of the captaincy, it was less busy than that of Santa Cruz. Its last Manueline ruins, in Rua da Árvore, were demolished in 1916.
location: Rua da Árvore, Machico

name: Fortaleza de S. Lourenço
summary: The Fortress of São Lourenço in Funchal was begun under King Manuel I and completed under Philippine rule. It was stormed by French pirates in 1566 and later housed a chapel and various public buildings.
location: Funchal

name: Lombo de São João
summary: Lombo de São João is an inhabited locality in the parish of Ribeira Brava. It is named after its chapel of São João Baptista, which was rebuilt in 1750.
location: sítio in the parish and municipality of Ribeira Brava

name: Hospital de S. Lazaro
summary: The Hospital de São Lázaro was Funchal's leper hospital, probably founded in the late fifteenth century and maintained by the Câmara. It closed in 1912, after which its building became the civil prison. The entry also records medical opinions on leprosy (elephantiasis) in Madeira.
location: Funchal

name: Teatro de Bom Gosto
summary: The Teatro de Bom Gosto was a small theatre in Funchal, built around 1818–1820 near the Teatro Grande. It was owned by the first Count of Carvalhal, who had it refurbished after 1834. The last known performance there took place in 1838.
location: Funchal, near the Teatro Grande

name: Porto Santo
summary: Porto Santo, also called Baleira, is the town and municipality of the island of Porto Santo and was the seat of a captaincy. The Elucidário covers its lost foral and its nineteenth-century administrative reorganisation.
location: town and municipality of Porto Santo, island of Porto Santo

name: Habitações primitivas
summary: This entry describes the first dwellings built on Madeira after its discovery, made of local timber such as cedar. It also records traditions about the first two-storey house and the first stone house in Funchal.
location: Madeira

name: Capelas de Santa Isabel
summary: This entry describes two chapels dedicated to Saint Elizabeth. One is inside the Misericórdia building in Funchal, probably built in the early eighteenth century and noted for its gilded carved altar; the other is attached to the hospital of Santa Cruz.
location: Misericórdia building, Funchal, and the hospital of Santa Cruz

name: Colégio e Igreja de São João Evangelista
aliases: São João Evangelista (Colégio e Igreja de)
summary: The Jesuit college and church of São João Evangelista in Funchal date from the Jesuits' arrival in 1570, with the building constructed in the seventeenth century. It was later used as a seminary, barracks and public offices, and the church was restored in 1847. The entry reproduces eighteenth-century descriptions of the chapels, their founders and benefactors.
location: Funchal

name: Chão
summary: Ilhéu Chão is the smallest and flattest of the Desertas islands, and the one nearest to Ponta de São Lourenço.
location: Desertas, nearest to Ponta de São Lourenço

name: Lambert
summary: The Quinta Lambert, or Quinta das Angústias, was a celebrated estate in Funchal whose house and chapel hosted royal visitors, including Queen Adelaide, the Duke of Leuchtenberg and the Empress Amélia of Brazil. The Empress's daughter, Princess Maria Amélia, died there in 1853. The estate was bought by Dr Júlio Paulo de Freitas in 1903.
location: quinta in Funchal

name: Padrões Memoráveis
summary: This entry surveys places and buildings in Madeira regarded as 'memorable landmarks' of Portuguese discovery and settlement. They are the island itself, the Desembarcadouro at Machico, the Santa Catarina chapel, Santa Clara church, the Quinta das Cruzes and the Senhor dos Milagres chapel at Machico.
location: Madeira, including Machico

name: Ponta da Ponta do Pargo
summary: Ponta do Pargo is the rugged headland forming Madeira's westernmost point. It is the site of the lighthouse.
location: headland in the parish of Ponta do Pargo, westernmost point of Madeira

name: Rua da Princesa D. Maria Amelia
summary: Rua da Princesa D. Maria Amélia is a Funchal street named by the municipal council in 1852 to mark Princess Maria Amélia's visit to Madeira. It links Rua da Imperatriz D. Amélia with the area near the Pontinha.
location: street in Funchal, between Rua da Imperatriz D. Amélia and the Pontinha

name: São Vicente
summary: São Vicente is a town and municipality on Madeira's north coast. It was raised to a town (vila) by royal charter in 1744 to free the northern parishes from distant Machico, and was reorganised as a municipality in 1835. The entry also covers later boundary changes involving Porto Moniz and plans to move the municipal seat.
location: town and municipality of São Vicente, north coast of Madeira

name: Leite Monteiro
summary: Leite Monteiro Park is a public park at Monte, above Funchal. It was begun by the municipal council in 1894 and named after the council president, Dr José Leite Monteiro. It contains the marble Fonte de Nossa Senhora, whose 18th-century inscription records Charles Murray's purchase of its water.
location: Park at Monte, parish of Monte, municipality of Funchal, Madeira

name: Castelo de S. João do Pico
summary: The Castle of São João do Pico is a fortress on the Pico dos Frias, north-west of Funchal, overlooking the city and its harbour. The Elucidário records that it was built between 1622 and 1640 and later served for a time as the district prison.
location: On the Pico dos Frias, north-west of Funchal, municipality of Funchal, Madeira

name: Arco de São Jorge
summary: Arco de São Jorge is a small parish on the north coast of Madeira, lying between São Jorge and Boaventura, and was created in 1676. The Elucidário covers its church history, fertility and climate, and notable natives. It also describes the remarkable landslide of 1689 that formed the Quebrada.
location: Parish on the north coast, between São Jorge and Boaventura, municipality of Santana, Madeira

name: Fortaleza de S. Tiago
summary: The Fortress of São Tiago stands on a rocky point east of Funchal harbour. It was built during the Philippine period (dated 1614) and later enlarged and rebuilt in 1767. It housed British gunners during the English occupation and, in 1921, a mountain artillery battery.
location: On a rocky point east of Funchal harbour, municipality of Funchal, Madeira

name: Aviceiro ou Fonte do Aviceiro
summary: Aviceiro, or Fonte do Aviceiro, is a locality in the parish of Santo António, near Lombo de D. Isabel. It lies on the road leading to Curral das Freiras.
location: Sítio near Lombo de D. Isabel, parish of Santo António, municipality of Funchal, Madeira

name: Avenida do Doutor Jose Antonio de Almada
aliases: Doutor Jose Antonio de Almada (Avenida do)
summary: The Avenida do Doutor José António de Almada is an avenue in Funchal named after Dr José António de Almada. Formerly the Pontinha road, it was built around 1874 along the coast south of the Vigias and Lambert quintas.
location: Along the coast south of the Vigias and Lambert quintas, Funchal, Madeira

name: Albergaria e Capela de S. Bartolomeu
aliases: Albergaria e Capela de S. Bartolomeu
summary: The Albergaria de S. Bartolomeu was a hostel for poor clergy in Funchal, with an adjoining chapel of São Bartolomeu. It was founded by Gonçalo Anes de Velosa in 1497. The first Jesuits lodged there before their college was founded.
location: Funchal, municipality of Funchal, Madeira

name: Lombo de São João
summary: Lombo de São João is a populated locality in the parish of Ponta do Sol, named after its chapel of São João. The chapel was an entailed property of the Berenguer de França family, whose head took the title of viscount of São João from the place.
location: Sítio in the parish of Ponta do Sol, municipality of Ponta do Sol, Madeira
